entries.search: A brief respite on the escape route from Suslanger’s captivity. This is a transitional scene rather than an independent settlement; the connected locations show where the journey continues. Soldiers beat Kir nearly to death. In the slave pen, [[character/merc2]] nurses him back to consciousness, shortens his name to Kir and offers a partnership in escape. He initially hopes to explain the mistake to the authorities; the [[character/clerk|official]] instead assigns work according to the prisoners’ abilities. Kel has overheard that an officer possesses a map of the catacombs. Their escape coincides with the Horror’s attack on the slave camp: guards die and the camp burns. They obtain the map and take the catacombs out of the fortress area. Kel, usually so confident, admits her unease about the dark underground route. Once outside, Kel proposes refuge with an acquaintance who collects spiders. Their relationship begins in this shared dependence: Kir needs her local knowledge, and Kel needs a partner.

entries.search: [[character/daughter]] guards Estera’s cave while the witch is away. Her exchanges with Kir and Kel include a rivalry over a necklace and directions to the Old Dragon. She also helps explain why the Magic Orb has lost its power after use, making her part of the search for a way to consult it again. [[character/daughter]] guards the cave while Estera is visiting the [[character/skd|Old Dragon]]. Her quarrel with Kel over a necklace exposes Kel’s jealousy and Kir’s failure to notice it. Airy refuses his courtship and suggests looking at the person already beside him. At the dragon’s lair, Estera is the troublesome visitor rather than a prisoner: she refuses to leave without information about a flower. Kir obtains it and the witch goes home. [[character/witch]] then admits the Orb was stolen by orcs; Airy identifies the islands and warns that it lost its power after its earlier use. The stolen Orb stands on an island orc pedestal. Kir obtains the bridge gear from their gathering on Council Mountain to reach it. Once Babur is safe and has seen the damaged Orb, he provides the key to the observatory approach. The observatory book lets Estera prescribe washing the Orb in underground spring water. A landslide closes Kir’s former route to Tka-Rik, forcing him through the old tunnel. Before departure, Airy asks Kel to greet the Chosen if they meet him and says she still remembers him. Kel apologises for her earlier jealousy; both women recognise feelings Kir has yet to understand. The repaired Orb shows snow rather than Jigran. Tka-Rik interprets this as Ingos, agrees that Kel can go with Kir, and warns that greater freedom there does not prevent cruel government or make their search for powerful magic safe.

entries.search: [[character/merc10]] is Feiruz’s fiancée and a contact of the Last Shelter. After escaping prison and losing him, she leads Kir and Kel to the brotherhood and vouches for them before [[character/glav]]. She also asks them to find the missing [[character/merc7]] and obtain medicine for her recovery. Feiruz asks Kir to repay his help by rescuing his imprisoned fiancée [[character/merc10]]. He dies during the escape. Kel urges the grieving Aliya to avenge him and identifies the man who struck the fatal blow. Kir objects to deliberate revenge, but their companions insist on their code. The death of the prison commandant brings searches across the city. Fearing for his collection, Rindeil withdraws his protection, though he says Kir may return once the danger passes. Aliya then leads Kir and Kel to the Last Shelter and speaks for them before [[character/glav]]. Khatul demands an imperial signet ring from a cyclops as a test of trust. Kir brings it back and explains his intention to free his family. He also recognises that the ring does not match the description he has read. Khatul already knows it is false, but asks him to preserve the brotherhood’s belief in the trophy. Membership changes how [[character/zaku]] receives Kir: the smith who refused a stranger now offers his craft. Through Aliya, Kir also searches for the missing [[character/merc7]], rescues her and brings medicine. Sahilia’s recovery matters later, when her forged papers open a route into the army.

entries.search: [[character/baron]] commands the Canian holdouts on Jigran against Firez’s Khadaganian forces. Proud of his family, he dislikes asking for aid even after losing Dar-Ulgorn. Kir’s arrival, the fight against the undead and the recruitment of powerful allies give his army a chance to attack Firez’s stronghold. He imagines a restored, prosperous Jigran ruled by his descendants. The old portal brings the travellers to the Canian side of Jigran, where [[character/baron]] questions their arrival amid attacks by the undead. The baron has lost Dar-Ulgorn to Firez’s forces but refuses Kir’s suggestion to seek outside help, citing his family’s pride. Kir and Kel assist the endangered settlements. They meet the baron’s son [[character/bson]] and the overworked [[character/stark]]. Stark provides a password for [[character/doctor]], a seller of sweets who secretly gathers intelligence for the baron. These local alliances make the campaign against Firez possible. The trail of the local undead leads to [[character/nekro]] on Death Island. Brought before the baron, he bargains for his life with the promise of useful knowledge. Kir and Kel obtain a potion from a tomb, but need to know how to apply it across the affected area. Jaminin first entertains a human sacrifice; Kel rejects it, and he supplies a less destructive method involving cemetery soil and an incantation. The potion puts the dead to rest. His later exchanges preserve the distinction between theoretical learning and practical competence: he possesses information, but his own experiment caused the disaster. Their success also changes the baron’s view of Kel. He admits that her achievements have repeatedly disproved his claim that war is no business for women. Dartas treats Kel as someone he is entitled to possess, insults her attachment to Kir and refuses to accept rejection. When Kir confronts him, Dartas asks what he wants in exchange for her and then calls him a coward. They duel on Death Island. Defeated and spared, Dartas admits despair over Dar-Ulgorn’s loss and his family’s future. Kir answers with his own enslavement, escape and determination to fight, winning Dartas’s respect. Kel initially believes the duel means that Kir has recognised her feelings; he disappoints her by calling it a defence of his own honour. The baron considers punishment, then accepts that Dartas needed the lesson; Kir asks him not to punish his son further. Kir proposes a special weapon alloy against the undead, drawing on a book he read. Stark sends him to an abandoned forge rather than allow a youngster to work in his own smithy. When Kir returns with the alloy, Kel recognises the source of the craftsman’s resistance: a hereditary master is ashamed of learning something his father never taught him. Kir presents the discovery as knowledge Stark can pass to his own son. The smith agrees to try it, and the baron welcomes the advantage for his soldiers. The improved weapons strengthen his preparations for an offensive. Rad leaves his troop report in a cemetery cache; collecting herbs gives him an innocent reason to visit it. Kir and Kel deliver the report, gather poisonous mushrooms and a pumpkin for Rad’s stew, then take the prepared meal to the enemy mess hall. The pumpkin prolongs the mushrooms’ laxative effect, keeping defenders away from their posts during the assault. Uncle Rad’s intelligence and preparations distract the defenders of Dar-Ulgorn so the baron’s forces can retake the fortress. The victory restores the family’s former boundary, but Virril will not advance blindly into Khadaganian territory. Kir and Kel steal a detailed map from the enemy headquarters and deliver Rad’s report. The resulting offensive captures the river crossing and brings Firez within reach. Kel worries that the end of Kir’s family quest will also end their life together, while the baron imagines a prosperous Jigran under his descendants. The victory means different things to the people who share it. The sealed cache supplies Kir with Joon armour, but Tui-Len warns him against relying on hatred alone. He gives him an amulet that can turn dangerous creatures into allies. Rad identifies suitable hunting grounds for a cyclops and a dragon. Their recruitment changes the military balance and answers the baron’s objection that his soldiers cannot face Firez’s necromancy in a direct assault. Virril finally orders the attack. Before the confrontation, Rad speaks of the quiet home and family he hopes to have when his secret work is finished. The cache is found in the valley Rad hopes to settle after the war. Dartas’s account of a nearby village destroyed by harpies points Kir to the rectangular amulet needed at its sealed entrance; Tui-Len supplies the remaining magical help. During the assault, Firez sends the city’s population, transformed into undead, against the Canian force. Kir must break through this army to reach the palace.

entries.search: The Beastmasters’ settlement brings together Geraldine, Crooked, Trickster and Yam-Akara. Suspicion after the empty caravan tests the newcomers’ reception. The truth about Brissen’s death ultimately exposes a crime within this community. At the Beastmasters’ settlement, [[character/vor]] accuses Kir and Kel of being spies. [[character/gerald]] agrees to test them. Their attempt to obtain a gold nugget from a caravan finds an empty chest, making their return dangerous. [[character/mthief]] reasons that genuine thieves would not come back empty-handed, and Geraldine accepts them. Advice from Trickster, also passed on by Sver if Kir consults him, about an ice elemental in the abandoned mines provides something to offer Yam-Akara. His work and the governor’s permit requirements then draw the travellers into further dealings with the court. The missing nugget will matter again when the apparent caravan failure becomes evidence of a separate theft. Trickster notices that Geraldine repeatedly leaves the settlement in secret. As its leader, he argues, she should not keep matters from her people. He asks Kir and Kel to follow her. They see a meeting with a man, but magical traps prevent them from approaching unnoticed and frighten the pair away. Their first report therefore establishes a secret meeting, not the man’s identity. Suspicion later falls on both His and Karansul; the eventual explanation is Geraldine’s relationship with the merchant, whom she plans to marry. A knife found at the murder site appears to implicate His. The court magician admits it was stolen from his laboratory together with the governor’s nugget. He had sent out the empty caravan to hide that loss and hoped to blame raiders after an informant warned of the planned attack. His arranges a meeting to produce evidence, but is killed before he can clear himself. Meanwhile Geraldine and Karansul disclose their relationship and provide each other with an alibi. Their commercial hostility and private secrecy had made them suspicious without establishing guilt. The settlement’s missing communal money supplies the decisive motive. Kir and Kel catch Crooked at his cache. Brissen had discovered the theft, so Crooked killed him. He also stole His’s knife and the gold nugget, informed on the caravan raid and later planted the knife to shift suspicion. His called the same informant to clear his own name; Crooked mistook that invitation for a trap and killed him too. Woodsfolk observations help reconstruct the planted evidence. Before the governor, Kir explains the connected crimes and Crooked admits them. Yam-Akara is released, while the governor reserves Crooked’s punishment for trial. Kel draws the thief out by spreading word that they have found the hidden money. Afterwards the travellers return the recovered communal funds to Geraldine and Trickster. Geraldine wants personal revenge, but Crooked is already in the governor’s custody. During his confinement, Yam-Akara gains access to the governor’s library. Old exploration reports reveal that the powerful “artifact” is a forgotten passage to another land. Trickster offers a key to the gate, then sends Kir on a fruitless ore search so that he can work without interference. With the key ready, Yam-Akara warns that he cannot sense the destination: the portal may be defective or concealed by a powerful absorbing spell. Kir recognises the same absence Tka-Rik described and concludes that it leads to Jigran. He decides to go directly, trusting the strength gained during his journey. Kel chooses to accompany him again.

entries.search: The black market brings together craftspeople, illicit trade and local information. Master Arkhar and the fortune-teller offer very different services here. For conspicuous fugitives such as Kir and Kel, useful contacts are as valuable as equipment. Rindeil wants a meteorite sample brought from the lands the Khadaganians call useless. He has arranged to exchange it for a rare addition to his collection. Kir overhears the guards to locate the sample, but its locked chest calls for a better thief. Karim directs him to Feiruz at the Black Market. Kel challenges Feiruz’s pride until he agrees to help, on condition that they return the favour later. He opens the chest, earns Kel’s praise and leaves the party to rest. Rindeil rewards the delivery. The unpaid favour explains why Feiruz later expects help rescuing Aliya.

entries.search: The exit from the catacombs marks a transition between the underground escape route and the world outside. Its significance lies in the travellers’ progress through Suslanger, rather than a separate local community. Soldiers beat Kir nearly to death. In the slave pen, [[character/merc2]] nurses him back to consciousness, shortens his name to Kir and offers a partnership in escape. He initially hopes to explain the mistake to the authorities; the [[character/clerk|official]] instead assigns work according to the prisoners’ abilities. Kel has overheard that an officer possesses a map of the catacombs. Their escape coincides with the Horror’s attack on the slave camp: guards die and the camp burns. They obtain the map and take the catacombs out of the fortress area. Kel, usually so confident, admits her unease about the dark underground route. Once outside, Kel proposes refuge with an acquaintance who collects spiders. Their relationship begins in this shared dependence: Kir needs her local knowledge, and Kel needs a partner.

entries.search: Dar-Leanos is the Canian stronghold where Kir meets Baron Virril, his son Dartas and Master Stark. Losses in the war and recurring undead attacks shape its needs. The city becomes the base for the struggle to reach Firez and free Jigran. The old portal brings the travellers to the Canian side of Jigran, where [[character/baron]] questions their arrival amid attacks by the undead. The baron has lost Dar-Ulgorn to Firez’s forces but refuses Kir’s suggestion to seek outside help, citing his family’s pride. Kir and Kel assist the endangered settlements. They meet the baron’s son [[character/bson]] and the overworked [[character/stark]]. Stark provides a password for [[character/doctor]], a seller of sweets who secretly gathers intelligence for the baron. These local alliances make the campaign against Firez possible. The trail of the local undead leads to [[character/nekro]] on Death Island. Brought before the baron, he bargains for his life with the promise of useful knowledge. Kir and Kel obtain a potion from a tomb, but need to know how to apply it across the affected area. Jaminin first entertains a human sacrifice; Kel rejects it, and he supplies a less destructive method involving cemetery soil and an incantation. The potion puts the dead to rest. His later exchanges preserve the distinction between theoretical learning and practical competence: he possesses information, but his own experiment caused the disaster. Their success also changes the baron’s view of Kel. He admits that her achievements have repeatedly disproved his claim that war is no business for women. Dartas treats Kel as someone he is entitled to possess, insults her attachment to Kir and refuses to accept rejection. When Kir confronts him, Dartas asks what he wants in exchange for her and then calls him a coward. They duel on Death Island. Defeated and spared, Dartas admits despair over Dar-Ulgorn’s loss and his family’s future. Kir answers with his own enslavement, escape and determination to fight, winning Dartas’s respect. Kel initially believes the duel means that Kir has recognised her feelings; he disappoints her by calling it a defence of his own honour. The baron considers punishment, then accepts that Dartas needed the lesson; Kir asks him not to punish his son further. Kir proposes a special weapon alloy against the undead, drawing on a book he read. Stark sends him to an abandoned forge rather than allow a youngster to work in his own smithy. When Kir returns with the alloy, Kel recognises the source of the craftsman’s resistance: a hereditary master is ashamed of learning something his father never taught him. Kir presents the discovery as knowledge Stark can pass to his own son. The smith agrees to try it, and the baron welcomes the advantage for his soldiers. The improved weapons strengthen his preparations for an offensive. Rad leaves his troop report in a cemetery cache; collecting herbs gives him an innocent reason to visit it. Kir and Kel deliver the report, gather poisonous mushrooms and a pumpkin for Rad’s stew, then take the prepared meal to the enemy mess hall. The pumpkin prolongs the mushrooms’ laxative effect, keeping defenders away from their posts during the assault. Uncle Rad’s intelligence and preparations distract the defenders of Dar-Ulgorn so the baron’s forces can retake the fortress. The victory restores the family’s former boundary, but Virril will not advance blindly into Khadaganian territory. Kir and Kel steal a detailed map from the enemy headquarters and deliver Rad’s report. The resulting offensive captures the river crossing and brings Firez within reach. Kel worries that the end of Kir’s family quest will also end their life together, while the baron imagines a prosperous Jigran under his descendants. The victory means different things to the people who share it. Kel and Rad discover that Firez is moving the Joon prisoners from the mountain prison into his fortress. Kel plans an attack on the transfer, avoiding a direct prison assault. Among those freed are [[character/deva]], whom Kir admired as a child, and the elder [[character/junofil]]. Tai-Ilara welcomes his changed appearance and asks him to retrieve belongings left behind. Tui-Len brings harder news: Kir’s parents are dead. The elder fears that killing Firez will expose the survivors to the Curse, but Kir tells him that Tka-Rik and At-Zako have already destroyed it. Tui-Len also opens the sealed Joon cache whose amulet Kir has recovered. Seeing Kir reunited with Tai-Ilara, Kel asks for the way back to Suslanger. Kir begs her to stay and mentions one more expedition for Tai-Ilara’s belongings. Kel agrees because she still fears for him, calling it their last adventure together. She dies during that expedition. On Kir’s return, Tai-Ilara is concerned with her comb and mirror and dismisses his grief. Her reaction breaks his idealised childhood attachment. He recognises Kel as the person who was closest and most loyal to him, and realises that he failed to see her love while she was beside him. Kel can be resurrected in the original Lost in Astral campaign. Her scripted death still occurs, but if Kir has all three parts of the Rod of Life when he finishes the conversation with [[character/deva|Tai-Ilara]] about her retrieved belongings, [[character/junofil|Tui-Len]] offers to bring Kel back. Completing his conversation consumes the fragments and returns Kel alive to the playable party before the final battle, with her saved skills, experience and equipment. Speak to her afterward for their reunion: Kir finally declares his love and asks forgiveness for his blindness. Kel answers that his love matters more than everything else. The sealed cache supplies Kir with Joon armour, but Tui-Len warns him against relying on hatred alone. He gives him an amulet that can turn dangerous creatures into allies. Rad identifies suitable hunting grounds for a cyclops and a dragon. Their recruitment changes the military balance and answers the baron’s objection that his soldiers cannot face Firez’s necromancy in a direct assault. Virril finally orders the attack. Before the confrontation, Rad speaks of the quiet home and family he hopes to have when his secret work is finished. The cache is found in the valley Rad hopes to settle after the war. Dartas’s account of a nearby village destroyed by harpies points Kir to the rectangular amulet needed at its sealed entrance; Tui-Len supplies the remaining magical help. During the assault, Firez sends the city’s population, transformed into undead, against the Canian force. Kir must break through this army to reach the palace.

entries.search: The city of Ingos houses the governor, his court magician and the merchant Karansul. Their interests intersect with the murder inquiry: private relationships, a stolen nugget and the court’s own schemes all become relevant evidence. Kir and Kel seek magical help on Ingos. [[character/trader]] complains about [[character/kmage]], whose cheap runes undercut his trade, and identifies [[character/his]] as the governor’s court magician. His receives the travellers with suspicion and later asks them to retrieve materials from his laboratory. [[character/trapper]] offers another route: contact [[character/grey]] through the Sacred Flower and a vessel from his cache. Grey Leaf explains that the knight Brissen and his magician friend have left for the settlement near the mines. Kir’s first task here is finding an informed ally, before the murder that later dominates the investigation. The vessel Sver asks them to carry is for Woodsfolk balm that eases his own aching joints. He has used their necessary visit to obtain a personal favour. At the Beastmasters’ settlement, [[character/vor]] accuses Kir and Kel of being spies. [[character/gerald]] agrees to test them. Their attempt to obtain a gold nugget from a caravan finds an empty chest, making their return dangerous. [[character/mthief]] reasons that genuine thieves would not come back empty-handed, and Geraldine accepts them. Advice from Trickster, also passed on by Sver if Kir consults him, about an ice elemental in the abandoned mines provides something to offer Yam-Akara. His work and the governor’s permit requirements then draw the travellers into further dealings with the court. The missing nugget will matter again when the apparent caravan failure becomes evidence of a separate theft. Yam-Akara introduces himself as a practising magician of the first rank and an honorary member of the Assembly of Magicians of Three Worlds. The elemental samples interest him, and the Joon artifact promises material for a scholarly report. He agrees to search while Kir renews his permit for the mines, where Wormface magic interferes with his measurements. His summons the travellers to Governor Valrasian whether or not his own laboratory errand is complete. The governor demands proper introductions, pays unwelcome attention to Kel and hints at a rare Blue Clan mage’s dart for his collection. Bringing the dart wins the permit, despite his complaints about Yam-Akara’s visits. Green leaves around the settlement lead Kir to Grey Leaf, who brings the news. Brissen is murdered and Yam-Akara is accused of killing his old friend. Kir and Kel undertake the defence. The magician says he spent the day in the mines and arrived late for their meeting. [[character/guard]] confirms that he allowed the elderly visitor through with an expired permit and stamped it that day. Kir finds the lost pass, but [[character/huber]] rejects the water-damaged document because the signature and date can no longer be read. This evidence supports the search but does not free Yam-Akara; the travellers still have to identify the murderer. A knife found at the murder site appears to implicate His. The court magician admits it was stolen from his laboratory together with the governor’s nugget. He had sent out the empty caravan to hide that loss and hoped to blame raiders after an informant warned of the planned attack. His arranges a meeting to produce evidence, but is killed before he can clear himself. Meanwhile Geraldine and Karansul disclose their relationship and provide each other with an alibi. Their commercial hostility and private secrecy had made them suspicious without establishing guilt. The settlement’s missing communal money supplies the decisive motive. Kir and Kel catch Crooked at his cache. Brissen had discovered the theft, so Crooked killed him. He also stole His’s knife and the gold nugget, informed on the caravan raid and later planted the knife to shift suspicion. His called the same informant to clear his own name; Crooked mistook that invitation for a trap and killed him too. Woodsfolk observations help reconstruct the planted evidence. Before the governor, Kir explains the connected crimes and Crooked admits them. Yam-Akara is released, while the governor reserves Crooked’s punishment for trial. Kel draws the thief out by spreading word that they have found the hidden money. Afterwards the travellers return the recovered communal funds to Geraldine and Trickster. Geraldine wants personal revenge, but Crooked is already in the governor’s custody.

Khabburu then asks him to water a neglected tree beside the well in a military camp. Next he asks for a frightened animal from the village south of Karansul’s domain to be guided to the Woodsfolk. The animal is a cow, whose milk interests them. After these acts, Khabburu gives Kir a key dropped by a man he saw staggering and singing near the mines. The key helps solve the gates and levers barring an underground chest. Its contents include the third Rod of Life fragment. This chain is optional, but its completion can determine whether Kir later has the means to bring Kel back. A knife found at the murder site appears to implicate His. The court magician admits it was stolen from his laboratory together with the governor’s nugget. He had sent out the empty caravan to hide that loss and hoped to blame raiders after an informant warned of the planned attack. His arranges a meeting to produce evidence, but is killed before he can clear himself. Meanwhile Geraldine and Karansul disclose their relationship and provide each other with an alibi. entries.search: [[character/vor]] is hostile to Kir and Kel and accuses them of spying. The investigation ultimately exposes his theft from the settlement’s common funds. In his confession he admits killing Brissen after the knight discovered it, planting the stolen knife and killing His to prevent their dealings from being revealed. Advice from Trickster, also passed on by Sver if Kir consults him, about an ice elemental in the abandoned mines provides something to offer Yam-Akara. His work and the governor’s permit requirements then draw the travellers into further dealings with the court. The missing nugget will matter again when the apparent caravan failure becomes evidence of a separate theft. The settlement’s missing communal money supplies the decisive motive. Kir and Kel catch Crooked at his cache. Brissen had discovered the theft, so Crooked killed him. He also stole His’s knife and the gold nugget, informed on the caravan raid and later planted the knife to shift suspicion. entries.search: The old portal brings the travellers to the Canian side of Jigran, where [[character/baron]] questions their arrival amid attacks by the undead. The baron has lost Dar-Ulgorn to Firez’s forces but refuses Kir’s suggestion to seek outside help, citing his family’s pride. Kir and Kel assist the endangered settlements. They meet the baron’s son [[character/bson]] and the overworked [[character/stark]]. Stark provides a password for [[character/doctor]], a seller of sweets who secretly gathers intelligence for the baron. These local alliances make the campaign against Firez possible. The trail of the local undead leads to [[character/nekro]] on Death Island. Brought before the baron, he bargains for his life with the promise of useful knowledge. Kir and Kel obtain a potion from a tomb, but need to know how to apply it across the affected area. Jaminin first entertains a human sacrifice; Kel rejects it, and he supplies a less destructive method involving cemetery soil and an incantation. The potion puts the dead to rest. His later exchanges preserve the distinction between theoretical learning and practical competence: he possesses information, but his own experiment caused the disaster. Their success also changes the baron’s view of Kel. He admits that her achievements have repeatedly disproved his claim that war is no business for women. Kir proposes a special weapon alloy against the undead, drawing on a book he read. Stark sends him to an abandoned forge rather than allow a youngster to work in his own smithy. When Kir returns with the alloy, Kel recognises the source of the craftsman’s resistance: a hereditary master is ashamed of learning something his father never taught him. Kir presents the discovery as knowledge Stark can pass to his own son. The smith agrees to try it, and the baron welcomes the advantage for his soldiers. The improved weapons strengthen his preparations for an offensive.

entries.search: Rad leaves his troop report in a cemetery cache; collecting herbs gives him an innocent reason to visit it. Kir and Kel deliver the report, gather poisonous mushrooms and a pumpkin for Rad’s stew, then take the prepared meal to the enemy mess hall. The pumpkin prolongs the mushrooms’ laxative effect, keeping defenders away from their posts during the assault. Uncle Rad’s intelligence and preparations distract the defenders of Dar-Ulgorn so the baron’s forces can retake the fortress. The victory restores the family’s former boundary, but Virril will not advance blindly into Khadaganian territory. Kir and Kel steal a detailed map from the enemy headquarters and deliver Rad’s report. The resulting offensive captures the river crossing and brings Firez within reach. Kel worries that the end of Kir’s family quest will also end their life together, while the baron imagines a prosperous Jigran under his descendants. The victory means different things to the people who share it.

Kir’s resolve wins his trust. His recollection of a blue-stoned medallion and a village destroyed by harpies also provides a lead to Joon relics. Dartas treats Kel as someone he is entitled to possess, insults her attachment to Kir and refuses to accept rejection. When Kir confronts him, Dartas asks what he wants in exchange for her and then calls him a coward. They duel on Death Island. entries.search: On Gipath, [[character/orcc]] says his warriors destroyed the Khadaganian expedition. He remembers how Zak’s defeat of a supposed Demon showed that armoured outsiders could be killed, and hopes Kir will become a Chosen for his own tribe. Their welcome depends on helping the tribe, and Kir soon rescues the chief from a harpy and his wife from goblins. The ogre quest proposes overfeeding it: starving it would make it dangerous, while ordinary feeding would let it grow. At the end of this optional sequence, Kir notices the heavy object Uyka wears around her neck. She found it in the mountains and treats it as a possible charm against evil or lizards. Kir recognises it as a key and can buy it. It opens the way to the Hall of the Great in the lizardmen’s tomb, where the greatest chiefs were buried. entries.search: [[character/merc8]] is a thief who helps Kir conceal his conspicuous face beneath a cloth, using fear of disease as a disguise. Later he asks for help rescuing his fiancée [[character/merc10]] from prison. He dies during the escape, leaving Aliya grieving and determined to retaliate. Rindeil suggests a poison that would change Kir’s skin colour but could cause paralysis; Karim offers a recipe that would take months. Neither solves the urgent problem. [[character/merc8]] proposes wrapping Kir’s face in cloth: survivors of a recent disease already conceal their disfigurement that way. Kir helps him with a theft to obtain the fabric, and Feiruz rewards his assistance. The disguise initially fools even Rindeil. It lets Kir move among the Khadaganians while continuing the search for another Joon. When Kel returns, she mocks the expensive cloth as an extravagant way to impersonate a poor survivor. She also warns that Rindeil’s promises of help are less reliable than his interest in spiders, and rejoins Kir to keep others from taking advantage of him. Rindeil wants a meteorite sample brought from the lands the Khadaganians call useless. He has arranged to exchange it for a rare addition to his collection. Kir overhears the guards to locate the sample, but its locked chest calls for a better thief. Karim directs him to Feiruz at the Black Market. Kel challenges Feiruz’s pride until he agrees to help, on condition that they return the favour later. He opens the chest, earns Kel’s praise and leaves the party to rest. Rindeil rewards the delivery. The unpaid favour explains why Feiruz later expects help rescuing Aliya. Feiruz asks Kir to repay his help by rescuing his imprisoned fiancée [[character/merc10]]. He dies during the escape. Kel urges the grieving Aliya to avenge him and identifies the man who struck the fatal blow. Kir objects to deliberate revenge, but their companions insist on their code. The death of the prison commandant brings searches across the city. Fearing for his collection, Rindeil withdraws his protection, though he says Kir may return once the danger passes. Aliya then leads Kir and Kel to the Last Shelter and speaks for them before [[character/glav]].

entries.search: [[character/firez]] rules the Khadaganian side of Jigran and is the enemy Kir fled. In their confrontation he reveals that he too is a Joon, expelled for necromancy, and claims that his experiments were meant to defeat the Curse. He prolongs his life at Jigran’s expense, tracks Kir with a dragonet and threatens to turn him into an obedient undead servant. His professed concern for the Joons sits beside his enslavement and coercion of them. [[character/hero]], whose full name is Kir-A-Chit-La, is a young Joon enslaved under [[character/firez]] on [[allod/jigran]]. He escapes the castle, leaving his family behind, and hopes to return with help. Outside the castle, a [[character/first|recruiter]] mistakes him for someone expected at the camp. Kir conceals his identity and accepts travel papers for work on Suslanger. The apparent opening to freedom instead delivers him to imperial authorities. [[character/hwleader]] dismisses his papers, treats him as a slave and considers reporting the red-skinned stranger for a reward. In the throne room, Firez reveals that he too is a Joon and has watched Kir through a dragonet since the escape. He says his people expelled him for necromancy and claims that his rule protected them from the Curse. Kir answers with their enslavement, his parents’ deaths and the destruction of Jigran to prolong Firez’s life. The tyrant’s explanation is his own defence, not proof that the captivity was benevolent. He threatens to kill Kir, raise him as an obedient servant and use him against the baron. Their exchange leads into the final battle for Jigran. Firez shelters behind a lethal magical barrier. Kir disables its four controls before he can reach the necromancer; teleportation platforms and enchanted lion statues form part of the final arena. Killing Firez completes the last quest and ends the campaign.

entries.search: Gipath remains outside the great empires and is strewn with Joon ruins. entries.search: Ingos is nominally Canian, but its governor’s effective power scarcely extends beyond the city walls. Independent communities and Woodsfolk inhabit the surrounding snowlands. Kir and Kel arrive following the Magic Orb’s clue. Brissen’s murder, a staged caravan and conflicting alibis make their visit an investigation; the cleared magician Yam-Akara discovers the route to Jigran. Kir and Kel seek magical help on Ingos. [[character/trader]] complains about [[character/kmage]], whose cheap runes undercut his trade, and identifies [[character/his]] as the governor’s court magician. His receives the travellers with suspicion and later asks them to retrieve materials from his laboratory. [[character/trapper]] offers another route: contact [[character/grey]] through the Sacred Flower and a vessel from his cache. Grey Leaf explains that the knight Brissen and his magician friend have left for the settlement near the mines. Kir’s first task here is finding an informed ally, before the murder that later dominates the investigation. The vessel Sver asks them to carry is for Woodsfolk balm that eases his own aching joints. He has used their necessary visit to obtain a personal favour. Grey Leaf reports that animals are dying after drinking from the northern river. His healers cannot save them while Karansul’s factory keeps discharging poison into the water. Kel recognises that treating the animals alone cannot solve the problem. Karansul proudly confirms his ownership and describes a blasting powder used in his mines. Kir can obtain the powder and destroy the polluting works. Grey Leaf thanks him for ending the contamination. This request concerns the Woodsfolk’s protection of the forest, separately from the search for the Joon artifact. At the Beastmasters’ settlement, [[character/vor]] accuses Kir and Kel of being spies. [[character/gerald]] agrees to test them. Their attempt to obtain a gold nugget from a caravan finds an empty chest, making their return dangerous. [[character/mthief]] reasons that genuine thieves would not come back empty-handed, and Geraldine accepts them. Advice from Trickster, also passed on by Sver if Kir consults him, about an ice elemental in the abandoned mines provides something to offer Yam-Akara. His work and the governor’s permit requirements then draw the travellers into further dealings with the court. The missing nugget will matter again when the apparent caravan failure becomes evidence of a separate theft. Yam-Akara introduces himself as a practising magician of the first rank and an honorary member of the Assembly of Magicians of Three Worlds. The elemental samples interest him, and the Joon artifact promises material for a scholarly report. He agrees to search while Kir renews his permit for the mines, where Wormface magic interferes with his measurements. His summons the travellers to Governor Valrasian whether or not his own laboratory errand is complete. The governor demands proper introductions, pays unwelcome attention to Kel and hints at a rare Blue Clan mage’s dart for his collection. Bringing the dart wins the permit, despite his complaints about Yam-Akara’s visits. Kir can continue helping [[character/haburu]] after freeing the dogs kept near Karansul’s manufactories. The elder first rewards him with a clue to valuables behind a fence south of the city; Kir finds that he can crawl underneath. Khabburu then asks him to water a neglected tree beside the well in a military camp. Next he asks for a frightened animal from the village south of Karansul’s domain to be guided to the Woodsfolk. The animal is a cow, whose milk interests them. After these acts, Khabburu gives Kir a key dropped by a man he saw staggering and singing near the mines. The key helps solve the gates and levers barring an underground chest. Its contents include the third Rod of Life fragment. This chain is optional, but its completion can determine whether Kir later has the means to bring Kel back. Green leaves around the settlement lead Kir to Grey Leaf, who brings the news. Brissen is murdered and Yam-Akara is accused of killing his old friend. Kir and Kel undertake the defence. The magician says he spent the day in the mines and arrived late for their meeting. [[character/guard]] confirms that he allowed the elderly visitor through with an expired permit and stamped it that day. Kir finds the lost pass, but [[character/huber]] rejects the water-damaged document because the signature and date can no longer be read. This evidence supports the search but does not free Yam-Akara; the travellers still have to identify the murderer. A knife found at the murder site appears to implicate His. The court magician admits it was stolen from his laboratory together with the governor’s nugget. He had sent out the empty caravan to hide that loss and hoped to blame raiders after an informant warned of the planned attack. His arranges a meeting to produce evidence, but is killed before he can clear himself. Meanwhile Geraldine and Karansul disclose their relationship and provide each other with an alibi. Their commercial hostility and private secrecy had made them suspicious without establishing guilt. The settlement’s missing communal money supplies the decisive motive. Kir and Kel catch Crooked at his cache. Brissen had discovered the theft, so Crooked killed him. He also stole His’s knife and the gold nugget, informed on the caravan raid and later planted the knife to shift suspicion. His called the same informant to clear his own name; Crooked mistook that invitation for a trap and killed him too. Woodsfolk observations help reconstruct the planted evidence. Before the governor, Kir explains the connected crimes and Crooked admits them. Yam-Akara is released, while the governor reserves Crooked’s punishment for trial. Kel draws the thief out by spreading word that they have found the hidden money. Afterwards the travellers return the recovered communal funds to Geraldine and Trickster. Geraldine wants personal revenge, but Crooked is already in the governor’s custody. During his confinement, Yam-Akara gains access to the governor’s library. Old exploration reports reveal that the powerful “artifact” is a forgotten passage to another land. Trickster offers a key to the gate, then sends Kir on a fruitless ore search so that he can work without interference. With the key ready, Yam-Akara warns that he cannot sense the destination: the portal may be defective or concealed by a powerful absorbing spell. Kir recognises the same absence Tka-Rik described and concludes that it leads to Jigran. He decides to go directly, trusting the strength gained during his journey. Kel chooses to accompany him again.

entries.search: The trail of the local undead leads to [[character/nekro]] on Death Island. Brought before the baron, he bargains for his life with the promise of useful knowledge. Kir and Kel obtain a potion from a tomb, but need to know how to apply it across the affected area. Jaminin first entertains a human sacrifice; Kel rejects it, and he supplies a less destructive method involving cemetery soil and an incantation. The potion puts the dead to rest. His later exchanges preserve the distinction between theoretical learning and practical competence: he possesses information, but his own experiment caused the disaster. Their success also changes the baron’s view of Kel. He admits that her achievements have repeatedly disproved his claim that war is no business for women. Dartas treats Kel as someone he is entitled to possess, insults her attachment to Kir and refuses to accept rejection. When Kir confronts him, Dartas asks what he wants in exchange for her and then calls him a coward. They duel on Death Island. Defeated and spared, Dartas admits despair over Dar-Ulgorn’s loss and his family’s future. Kir answers with his own enslavement, escape and determination to fight, winning Dartas’s respect. Kel initially believes the duel means that Kir has recognised her feelings; he disappoints her by calling it a defence of his own honour. The baron considers punishment, then accepts that Dartas needed the lesson; Kir asks him not to punish his son further.

entries.search: Jigran is Kir’s homeland, a closed allod caught in perpetual autumn and war between Canian and Khadaganian forces. Firez’s necromancy has drained its fields and forests; much of the population shelters in fortified towns while undead roam outside. Kir returns through an old passage with Kel, joins the struggle led by Baron Virril and discovers the fate of the Joons he left behind. [[character/hero]], whose full name is Kir-A-Chit-La, is a young Joon enslaved under [[character/firez]] on [[allod/jigran]]. He escapes the castle, leaving his family behind, and hopes to return with help. Outside the castle, a [[character/first|recruiter]] mistakes him for someone expected at the camp. Kir conceals his identity and accepts travel papers for work on Suslanger. The apparent opening to freedom instead delivers him to imperial authorities. [[character/hwleader]] dismisses his papers, treats him as a slave and considers reporting the red-skinned stranger for a reward. The old portal brings the travellers to the Canian side of Jigran, where [[character/baron]] questions their arrival amid attacks by the undead. The baron has lost Dar-Ulgorn to Firez’s forces but refuses Kir’s suggestion to seek outside help, citing his family’s pride. Kir and Kel assist the endangered settlements. They meet the baron’s son [[character/bson]] and the overworked [[character/stark]]. Stark provides a password for [[character/doctor]], a seller of sweets who secretly gathers intelligence for the baron. These local alliances make the campaign against Firez possible. Kir and Kel obtain a potion from a tomb, but need to know how to apply it across the affected area. Jaminin first entertains a human sacrifice; Kel rejects it, and he supplies a less destructive method involving cemetery soil and an incantation. The potion puts the dead to rest. His later exchanges preserve the distinction between theoretical learning and practical competence: he possesses information, but his own experiment caused the disaster. Their success also changes the baron’s view of Kel. He admits that her achievements have repeatedly disproved his claim that war is no business for women. Dartas treats Kel as someone he is entitled to possess, insults her attachment to Kir and refuses to accept rejection. When Kir confronts him, Dartas asks what he wants in exchange for her and then calls him a coward. They duel on Death Island. Defeated and spared, Dartas admits despair over Dar-Ulgorn’s loss and his family’s future. Kir answers with his own enslavement, escape and determination to fight, winning Dartas’s respect. Kel initially believes the duel means that Kir has recognised her feelings; he disappoints her by calling it a defence of his own honour. The baron considers punishment, then accepts that Dartas needed the lesson; Kir asks him not to punish his son further. Kir proposes a special weapon alloy against the undead, drawing on a book he read. Stark sends him to an abandoned forge rather than allow a youngster to work in his own smithy. When Kir returns with the alloy, Kel recognises the source of the craftsman’s resistance: a hereditary master is ashamed of learning something his father never taught him. Kir presents the discovery as knowledge Stark can pass to his own son. The smith agrees to try it, and the baron welcomes the advantage for his soldiers. The improved weapons strengthen his preparations for an offensive. Rad leaves his troop report in a cemetery cache; collecting herbs gives him an innocent reason to visit it. Kir and Kel deliver the report, gather poisonous mushrooms and a pumpkin for Rad’s stew, then take the prepared meal to the enemy mess hall. The pumpkin prolongs the mushrooms’ laxative effect, keeping defenders away from their posts during the assault. Uncle Rad’s intelligence and preparations distract the defenders of Dar-Ulgorn so the baron’s forces can retake the fortress. The victory restores the family’s former boundary, but Virril will not advance blindly into Khadaganian territory. Kir and Kel steal a detailed map from the enemy headquarters and deliver Rad’s report. The resulting offensive captures the river crossing and brings Firez within reach. Kel worries that the end of Kir’s family quest will also end their life together, while the baron imagines a prosperous Jigran under his descendants. The victory means different things to the people who share it. Kel and Rad discover that Firez is moving the Joon prisoners from the mountain prison into his fortress. Kel plans an attack on the transfer, avoiding a direct prison assault. Among those freed are [[character/deva]], whom Kir admired as a child, and the elder [[character/junofil]]. Tai-Ilara welcomes his changed appearance and asks him to retrieve belongings left behind. Tui-Len brings harder news: Kir’s parents are dead. The elder fears that killing Firez will expose the survivors to the Curse, but Kir tells him that Tka-Rik and At-Zako have already destroyed it. Tui-Len also opens the sealed Joon cache whose amulet Kir has recovered. Seeing Kir reunited with Tai-Ilara, Kel asks for the way back to Suslanger. Kir begs her to stay and mentions one more expedition for Tai-Ilara’s belongings. Kel agrees because she still fears for him, calling it their last adventure together. She dies during that expedition. On Kir’s return, Tai-Ilara is concerned with her comb and mirror and dismisses his grief. Her reaction breaks his idealised childhood attachment. He recognises Kel as the person who was closest and most loyal to him, and realises that he failed to see her love while she was beside him. Kel can be resurrected in the original Lost in Astral campaign. Her scripted death still occurs, but if Kir has all three parts of the Rod of Life when he finishes the conversation with [[character/deva|Tai-Ilara]] about her retrieved belongings, [[character/junofil|Tui-Len]] offers to bring Kel back. Completing his conversation consumes the fragments and returns Kel alive to the playable party before the final battle, with her saved skills, experience and equipment. Speak to her afterward for their reunion: Kir finally declares his love and asks forgiveness for his blindness. Kel answers that his love matters more than everything else. The sealed cache supplies Kir with Joon armour, but Tui-Len warns him against relying on hatred alone. He gives him an amulet that can turn dangerous creatures into allies. Rad identifies suitable hunting grounds for a cyclops and a dragon. Their recruitment changes the military balance and answers the baron’s objection that his soldiers cannot face Firez’s necromancy in a direct assault. Virril finally orders the attack. Before the confrontation, Rad speaks of the quiet home and family he hopes to have when his secret work is finished. The cache is found in the valley Rad hopes to settle after the war. Dartas’s account of a nearby village destroyed by harpies points Kir to the rectangular amulet needed at its sealed entrance; Tui-Len supplies the remaining magical help. During the assault, Firez sends the city’s population, transformed into undead, against the Canian force. Kir must break through this army to reach the palace. In the throne room, Firez reveals that he too is a Joon and has watched Kir through a dragonet since the escape. He says his people expelled him for necromancy and claims that his rule protected them from the Curse. Kir answers with their enslavement, his parents’ deaths and the destruction of Jigran to prolong Firez’s life. The tyrant’s explanation is his own defence, not proof that the captivity was benevolent. He threatens to kill Kir, raise him as an obedient servant and use him against the baron. Their exchange leads into the final battle for Jigran. Firez shelters behind a lethal magical barrier. Kir disables its four controls before he can reach the necromancer; teleportation platforms and enchanted lion statues form part of the final arena. Killing Firez completes the last quest and ends the campaign.

entries.search: [[character/sheriff]] serves Rindeil and formerly performed on stage. He tells Kir about a red-skinned youth once held by the scholars and locates a report in the necromancers’ citadel. Karim bribes a guard to open the gate and get the other guards drunk, but the plan fails. Kir and Kel nevertheless retrieve the report, which points Kir toward another Joon. [[character/elder]] welcomes Kel and her companion to his estate. Kir’s learning gives them common ground, though the collector’s chief concern remains his spiders. [[character/sheriff]], who manages the household and formerly performed on stage, remembers a report about a red-skinned youth and promises to investigate. Rindeil’s hospitality gives the fugitives a base, but Kir realises that the slave records still identify them. With Rindeil’s guidance, he steals the records from the authorities. This removes one immediate threat without concealing his conspicuous appearance. Rindeil suggests a poison that would change Kir’s skin colour but could cause paralysis; Karim offers a recipe that would take months. Neither solves the urgent problem. [[character/merc8]] proposes wrapping Kir’s face in cloth: survivors of a recent disease already conceal their disfigurement that way. Kir helps him with a theft to obtain the fabric, and Feiruz rewards his assistance. The disguise initially fools even Rindeil. It lets Kir move among the Khadaganians while continuing the search for another Joon. When Kel returns, she mocks the expensive cloth as an extravagant way to impersonate a poor survivor. She also warns that Rindeil’s promises of help are less reliable than his interest in spiders, and rejoins Kir to keep others from taking advantage of him. Rindeil wants a meteorite sample brought from the lands the Khadaganians call useless. He has arranged to exchange it for a rare addition to his collection. Kir overhears the guards to locate the sample, but its locked chest calls for a better thief. Karim directs him to Feiruz at the Black Market. Kel challenges Feiruz’s pride until he agrees to help, on condition that they return the favour later. He opens the chest, earns Kel’s praise and leaves the party to rest. Rindeil rewards the delivery. The unpaid favour explains why Feiruz later expects help rescuing Aliya. Karim locates a report about the missing red-skinned youth in the necromancers’ citadel. He has bribed a guard to open the gate and get the other guards drunk, but the watch remains alert. Kir and Kel retrieve the document despite the failed arrangement, and Kir defends Karim when Kel blames him. The report records transformation and teleportation before the attack on the scholars’ mansion, with Gipath as the destination. Kir decides to follow that Joon. Sahilia initially warns against joining the army, then has convincing enlistment papers forged while Kir empties her dangerous caches for her. Kel refuses to be left behind, passing as a young man herself. [[character/sergant]] puts them through military training in Death Canyon. Their performance earns a courier assignment to the Gipath expedition. Sealed orders and a portal pass finally let them leave Suslanger under the authority of the same empire that enslaved them.

entries.search: [[character/merc2]] is a thief from [[allod/suslanger]] and [[character/hero|Kir’s]] travelling companion in Lost in Astral. She saves his life in the slave pen, helps him escape and accompanies him through Gipath and Ingos to Jigran. Her contacts, quick thinking and willingness to challenge him make her an active partner in his search. She falls in love with him, although he is slow to recognise it. Kel can be resurrected after her scripted death: the optional Rod of Life route returns her to the party. The guide below explains the three fragments and the conversation that decides her fate. Kel hides concern behind jokes, taunts and a habit of speaking about herself in the third person. She spots expensive tricks and wounded pride quickly: Kir’s costly disguise amuses her, Feiruz’s vanity gives her a way to recruit him, and Stark’s reluctance to learn becomes obvious to her. Her loyalty also has limits and demands of its own. After Feiruz’s death she insists on vengeance under the thieves’ code, despite Kir’s objections. When Dartas insults her, she rejects pity and makes her anger clear. Her affection for Kir does not erase her judgement or her ties to other people. Soldiers beat Kir nearly to death. In the slave pen, [[character/merc2]] nurses him back to consciousness, shortens his name to Kir and offers a partnership in escape. He initially hopes to explain the mistake to the authorities; the [[character/clerk|official]] instead assigns work according to the prisoners’ abilities. Kel has overheard that an officer possesses a map of the catacombs. Their escape coincides with the Horror’s attack on the slave camp: guards die and the camp burns. They obtain the map and take the catacombs out of the fortress area. Kel, usually so confident, admits her unease about the dark underground route. Once outside, Kel proposes refuge with an acquaintance who collects spiders. Their relationship begins in this shared dependence: Kir needs her local knowledge, and Kel needs a partner. After the escape, Kel directs Kir to [[character/elder|Rindeil’s]] house. She knows enough of his habits to warn Kir that promises of help come second to his spiders. When she sees Kir’s new face wrapping, she points out how much money he has spent on looking poor and rejoins him to keep other rogues from exploiting him. Later, the locked meteorite chest requires [[character/merc8|Feiruz’s]] skill. Kel turns his refusal into a challenge to his nerve and reputation as a thief. His agreement creates a debt that draws them into the rescue of [[character/merc10]]. Feiruz dies during Aliya’s rescue. Kel has seen who struck the fatal blow and tells the grieving Aliya to rally their comrades. Kir objects to another killing, but Kel insists that the thieves must avenge one of their own. The episode shows a harder side of the woman who saved him: she can be tender toward Kir and uncompromising about obligations he does not share. Their journey takes them from Suslanger through [[allod/gipat]] and [[allod/ingos]]. When the hidden road to Jigran finally appears, Kel admits that the unknown destination frightens her. Kir decides to go immediately, believing that he now has the strength to face Firez himself. She corrects his assumption that he will travel alone: they are going together. Kir had expected her to remain with [[character/mthief|Trickster]], but she tells him she prefers him. Her decision brings her into a war for a homeland that is his, not hers. The baron considers punishment, then accepts that Dartas needed the lesson; Kir asks him not to punish his son further. Kel contributes more than another weapon to Kir’s cause. When [[character/stark]] resists the new alloy, she identifies his pride as the obstacle: accepting Kir’s discovery would mean admitting a gap in his own knowledge. Later, she asks [[character/doctor|Uncle Rad]] to investigate the Joon prisoners. Learning that Firez is transferring them from the mountain prison to his fortress, she proposes intercepting the convoy. This gives Kir a practical plan at the moment his fear for his family threatens his confidence. In gratitude he promises her a kiss; she makes sure he knows she will remember. While [[character/baron|Virril]] celebrates his military success and imagines his descendants ruling Jigran, Kel worries that freeing Kir’s family will end their journey together. She tells the baron that her own wish is simply to stay near Kir and have him notice her more often. His reunion with [[character/deva|Tai-Ilara]] seems to confirm her fear. Kel asks for the portal home, yet agrees to accompany him once more because she believes he is about to risk his life for Tai-Ilara’s belongings. Her decision to stay grows out of concern for him even as she prepares to leave. Seeing Kir reunited with Tai-Ilara, Kel asks for the way back to Suslanger. Kir begs her to stay and mentions one more expedition for Tai-Ilara’s belongings. Kel agrees because she still fears for him, calling it their last adventure together. She dies during that expedition. On Kir’s return, Tai-Ilara is concerned with her comb and mirror and dismisses his grief. Her reaction breaks his idealised childhood attachment. He recognises Kel as the person who was closest and most loyal to him, and realises that he failed to see her love while she was beside him. Kel can be resurrected in the original Lost in Astral campaign. Her scripted death still occurs, but if Kir has all three parts of the Rod of Life when he finishes the conversation with [[character/deva|Tai-Ilara]] about her retrieved belongings, [[character/junofil|Tui-Len]] offers to bring Kel back. Completing his conversation consumes the fragments and returns Kel alive to the playable party before the final battle, with her saved skills, experience and equipment. Speak to her afterward for their reunion: Kir finally declares his love and asks forgiveness for his blindness. Kel answers that his love matters more than everything else. Follow [[character/skelet|the fortune-teller’s]] optional chain of predictions on [[allod/suslanger]]. It ends at the enchanted levers in the Wormface underground passages, in “The Wormfaces’ Riddle”. Solve the puzzle and open the reward chest to obtain the first fragment. Complete this before leaving Suslanger for Gipath; the earlier predictions lead to the final puzzle. Follow [[character/spletnica|Uyka’s]] optional stories and errands on [[allod/gipat]] until she offers to sell the key she wears around her neck. It opens the way to the “Hall of the Great” in the lizardmen’s tomb. Explore that hall and take the second fragment from its reward chest before continuing to Ingos. Continue helping [[character/haburu|Khabburu]] on [[allod/ingos]]: free the dogs, follow his lead to the fenced cache, water the tree and bring the cow to the Woodsfolk. He eventually gives Kir a key connected to the mines. In “Groping in the Dark”, use it to solve the cave’s sequence of gates and levers, then open the final chest for the third fragment. Obtain it before travelling to Jigran. Keep all three fragments until you return to [[map/bz31j|the baron’s camp]] after Kel’s death. Finish the conversation with Tai-Ilara about the belongings you retrieved; the resurrection offer then begins if all three pieces are present. Complete Tui-Len’s conversation and speak to Kel for the reunion. If any fragment is missing at that first conversation’s conclusion, the story commits to the route without her. Finding a missing piece afterward does not reopen the offer; load a save from before the decision. The resurrection is handled through dialogue, so you do not need to craft or equip a usable staff.

entries.search: [[character/haburu]] is a Woodsfolk elder who remembers being imprisoned by humans and freed by another human. He urges Kir to judge individuals rather than whole peoples. His request to release caged dogs reflects the same belief that companions should choose their bonds freely. Kir can continue helping [[character/haburu]] after freeing the dogs kept near Karansul’s manufactories. The elder first rewards him with a clue to valuables behind a fence south of the city; Kir finds that he can crawl underneath. Khabburu then asks him to water a neglected tree beside the well in a military camp. Next he asks for a frightened animal from the village south of Karansul’s domain to be guided to the Woodsfolk. The animal is a cow, whose milk interests them. After these acts, Khabburu gives Kir a key dropped by a man he saw staggering and singing near the mines. The key helps solve the gates and levers barring an underground chest. Its contents include the third Rod of Life fragment. This chain is optional, but its completion can determine whether Kir later has the means to bring Kel back.
