entries.search: [[character/hero]], whose full name is Kir-A-Chit-La, is a young Joon enslaved under [[character/firez]] on [[allod/jigran]]. He escapes the castle, leaving his family behind, and hopes to return with help. Outside the castle, a [[character/first|recruiter]] mistakes him for someone expected at the camp. Kir conceals his identity and accepts travel papers for work on Suslanger. The apparent opening to freedom instead delivers him to imperial authorities. [[character/hwleader]] dismisses his papers, treats him as a slave and considers reporting the red-skinned stranger for a reward. Soldiers beat Kir nearly to death. In the slave pen, [[character/merc2]] nurses him back to consciousness, shortens his name to Kir and offers a partnership in escape. He initially hopes to explain the mistake to the authorities; the [[character/clerk|official]] instead assigns work according to the prisoners’ abilities. Kel has overheard that an officer possesses a map of the catacombs. Their escape coincides with the Horror’s attack on the slave camp: guards die and the camp burns. They obtain the map and take the catacombs out of the fortress area. Kel, usually so confident, admits her unease about the dark underground route. Once outside, Kel proposes refuge with an acquaintance who collects spiders. Their relationship begins in this shared dependence: Kir needs her local knowledge, and Kel needs a partner. [[character/elder]] welcomes Kel and her companion to his estate. Kir’s learning gives them common ground, though the collector’s chief concern remains his spiders. [[character/sheriff]], who manages the household and formerly performed on stage, remembers a report about a red-skinned youth and promises to investigate. Rindeil’s hospitality gives the fugitives a base, but Kir realises that the slave records still identify them. With Rindeil’s guidance, he steals the records from the authorities. This removes one immediate threat without concealing his conspicuous appearance. Rindeil suggests a poison that would change Kir’s skin colour but could cause paralysis; Karim offers a recipe that would take months. Neither solves the urgent problem. [[character/merc8]] proposes wrapping Kir’s face in cloth: survivors of a recent disease already conceal their disfigurement that way. Kir helps him with a theft to obtain the fabric, and Feiruz rewards his assistance. The disguise initially fools even Rindeil. It lets Kir move among the Khadaganians while continuing the search for another Joon. When Kel returns, she mocks the expensive cloth as an extravagant way to impersonate a poor survivor. She also warns that Rindeil’s promises of help are less reliable than his interest in spiders, and rejoins Kir to keep others from taking advantage of him. Rindeil wants a meteorite sample brought from the lands the Khadaganians call useless. He has arranged to exchange it for a rare addition to his collection. Kir overhears the guards to locate the sample, but its locked chest calls for a better thief. Karim directs him to Feiruz at the Black Market. Kel challenges Feiruz’s pride until he agrees to help, on condition that they return the favour later. He opens the chest, earns Kel’s praise and leaves the party to rest. Rindeil rewards the delivery. The unpaid favour explains why Feiruz later expects help rescuing Aliya. Feiruz asks Kir to repay his help by rescuing his imprisoned fiancée [[character/merc10]]. He dies during the escape. Kel urges the grieving Aliya to avenge him and identifies the man who struck the fatal blow. Kir objects to deliberate revenge, but their companions insist on their code. The death of the prison commandant brings searches across the city. Fearing for his collection, Rindeil withdraws his protection, though he says Kir may return once the danger passes. Aliya then leads Kir and Kel to the Last Shelter and speaks for them before [[character/glav]]. Khatul demands an imperial signet ring from a cyclops as a test of trust. Kir brings it back and explains his intention to free his family. He also recognises that the ring does not match the description he has read. Khatul already knows it is false, but asks him to preserve the brotherhood’s belief in the trophy. Membership changes how [[character/zaku]] receives Kir: the smith who refused a stranger now offers his craft. Through Aliya, Kir also searches for the missing [[character/merc7]], rescues her and brings medicine. Sahilia’s recovery matters later, when her forged papers open a route into the army. An imperial scout discovers the Shelter. After fighting the expedition, Khatul proposes placing Wormface bodies at the battlefield to conceal the brotherhood’s involvement. In the depths, [[character/guru]] recognises Kir as a Joon and invokes an ancient treaty. He demands the death of a necromancer disturbing the caves before granting access. Later he calls Kir mentally and offers information for rescuing the Priest of Silence from the necromancers. His account of a human searching for Joon remains gives another lead, though he cannot say where that man now lives. The alliance is reciprocal and conditional, not a promise to answer every question. While travelling through Suslanger in human guise, Kir can buy a succession of predictions from the [[character/skelet|fortune-teller]]. She first points him toward an orchard near the Portal, then toward a public building and an underground route. Further hints concern a harvest basket on the plantations, a chest beyond a fenced property, and an estate where undead appear at night. Kir challenges her obscure language but continues to investigate. The last prediction concerns the Wormface underground passages and a choice among enchanted mechanisms. Solving that puzzle can yield one of the fragments later identified as parts of the Rod of Life. These optional discoveries require Kir to act on the clues; the fortune-teller explicitly speaks of what may happen, not an inevitable future. Karim locates a report about the missing red-skinned youth in the necromancers’ citadel. He has bribed a guard to open the gate and get the other guards drunk, but the watch remains alert. Kir and Kel retrieve the document despite the failed arrangement, and Kir defends Karim when Kel blames him. The report records transformation and teleportation before the attack on the scholars’ mansion, with Gipath as the destination. Kir decides to follow that Joon. Sahilia initially warns against joining the army, then has convincing enlistment papers forged while Kir empties her dangerous caches for her. Kel refuses to be left behind, passing as a young man herself. [[character/sergant]] puts them through military training in Death Canyon. Their performance earns a courier assignment to the Gipath expedition. Sealed orders and a portal pass finally let them leave Suslanger under the authority of the same empire that enslaved them. On Gipath, [[character/orcc]] says his warriors destroyed the Khadaganian expedition. He remembers how Zak’s defeat of a supposed Demon showed that armoured outsiders could be killed, and hopes Kir will become a Chosen for his own tribe. Kel proposes a false report with unpromising stone samples to prevent another imperial expedition from being sent. The shaman [[character/orcpyr]] distrusts strangers but makes Kir a ritual axe after he supplies suitable stone, and makes beads for Kel. Their welcome depends on helping the tribe, and Kir soon rescues the chief from a harpy and his wife from goblins. Urk-Tar explains that humans have driven orcs out of the Foothills and are advancing into the Middle Mountains. Kir removes the Shell whose presence restrains the lizards, initially refusing to fight humans himself. When Tynachey describes the killing of the tribe’s inhabitants, Kel argues for helping their hosts recover the settlement, and Kir agrees. The [[character/iz|Hermit Lizard]] then offers news of the former Chosen in exchange for placing the Shell by the Remote Mountains’ lake. Restoring it also frees hunters held by lizards. The Hermit directs Kir toward the Great Magician by a route different from Zak’s old tunnel approach. Meeting [[character/rick]] gives Kir his first direct contact with a free Joon magician. Tka-Rik explains that At-Zako and Lu-a-Jalla are travelling together and that he himself remains bound to Gipath. He has never heard of Jigran. Kir tells him about Firez, his enslaved family and his promise to return. Learning that more Joons need help renews Tka-Rik’s purpose. Since he cannot locate the hidden allod unaided, he sends Kir to find the Magic Orb that At-Zako once used. Finding the magician therefore begins another investigation rather than immediately opening the road home. A [[character/loozer|messenger]] invites the rescuers of the hunters to [[character/karh]]’s camp. Bor claims neutrality in the war, yet asks them to act against the village’s hunters and caravans. To question [[character/smith]] about the Orb, Kir helps bring him out of the village. The letter can go to Babur himself or to the elder, with different explanations for the craftsman’s arrival. Babur then sends Kir to the lizards’ tomb for a supposed magical needle. The expedition supplies lizard hides, and Babur admits that useful armour material was his real interest. For information about the Orb, he redirects the visitors to Estera. Bor introduces Kir to [[character/spletnica]], who lives alone and receives household help in exchange for news. Her first story points toward the giant mushrooms near the goblin camp in the Middle Mountains; only one is edible. Later she reports that a survivor of the Khadaganian expedition left Estera’s refuge for the Distant Mountains. Kir worries that the man might return to Suslanger, and the resulting lead concerns treasure in the ruined expedition camp. Uyka also describes Go-Go as an imprisoned champion of goblin freedom and praises his supposed beauty. Kel is curious enough to consider visiting him, and the pair can free him from the island orcs. Uyka’s requests for repairs, provisions and money accompany these conversations; her account of someone’s motives or attractiveness remains her opinion. Further paid stories lead Kir to an animated skeleton’s severed legs in the Dead City and to a giant ogre being fattened by the island orcs. The ogre quest proposes overfeeding it: starving it would make it dangerous, while ordinary feeding would let it grow. At the end of this optional sequence, Kir notices the heavy object Uyka wears around her neck. She found it in the mountains and treats it as a possible charm against evil or lizards. Kir recognises it as a key and can buy it. It opens the way to the Hall of the Great in the lizardmen’s tomb, where the greatest chiefs were buried. Among its rewards is another fragment of the Rod of Life, giving Uyka’s local gossip a consequence far beyond Gipath. [[character/daughter]] guards the cave while Estera is visiting the [[character/skd|Old Dragon]]. Her quarrel with Kel over a necklace exposes Kel’s jealousy and Kir’s failure to notice it. Airy refuses his courtship and suggests looking at the person already beside him. At the dragon’s lair, Estera is the troublesome visitor rather than a prisoner: she refuses to leave without information about a flower. Kir obtains it and the witch goes home. [[character/witch]] then admits the Orb was stolen by orcs; Airy identifies the islands and warns that it lost its power after its earlier use. Airy’s warning about the depleted Orb leads Kir towards the observatory. Babur can open the blocked approach, but first demands the Chosen’s knife, now a sacred relic. While Kir pursues the relic, island orcs raid the hunters’ camp and carry Babur away. They hand him to their ogre neighbours after his dealings with them turn sour. Kir obtains the two keys to the pit, frees the craftsman and escorts him back alive. Babur renounces further trade with the orcs. His rescue also lets Bor put forward a new plan against the settlers. Bor’s final plan against the settlers uses the orcs’ old lightning pyramid. He supplies its key and asks Kir to activate it inside the new village, then escape its reach. The attack continues with orcs and Free Hunters finishing the surviving defenders. Kel calls the result a massacre and accuses Bor of using them for his dirty work. Bor answers that the settlers have retreated to the old village: he wanted to restore the balance disrupted by the Chosen. Kir understands that motive, while Kel’s objection remains part of the exchange. The restored order is Bor’s justification for the violence. The stolen Orb stands on an island orc pedestal. Kir obtains the bridge gear from their gathering on Council Mountain to reach it. Once Babur is safe and has seen the damaged Orb, he provides the key to the observatory approach. The observatory book lets Estera prescribe washing the Orb in underground spring water. A landslide closes Kir’s former route to Tka-Rik, forcing him through the old tunnel. Before departure, Airy asks Kel to greet the Chosen if they meet him and says she still remembers him. Kel apologises for her earlier jealousy; both women recognise feelings Kir has yet to understand. The repaired Orb shows snow rather than Jigran. Tka-Rik interprets this as Ingos, agrees that Kel can go with Kir, and warns that greater freedom there does not prevent cruel government or make their search for powerful magic safe. Kir and Kel seek magical help on Ingos. [[character/trader]] complains about [[character/kmage]], whose cheap runes undercut his trade, and identifies [[character/his]] as the governor’s court magician. His receives the travellers with suspicion and later asks them to retrieve materials from his laboratory. [[character/trapper]] offers another route: contact [[character/grey]] through the Sacred Flower and a vessel from his cache. Grey Leaf explains that the knight Brissen and his magician friend have left for the settlement near the mines. Kir’s first task here is finding an informed ally, before the murder that later dominates the investigation. The vessel Sver asks them to carry is for Woodsfolk balm that eases his own aching joints. He has used their necessary visit to obtain a personal favour. At the Beastmasters’ settlement, [[character/vor]] accuses Kir and Kel of being spies. [[character/gerald]] agrees to test them. Their attempt to obtain a gold nugget from a caravan finds an empty chest, making their return dangerous. [[character/mthief]] reasons that genuine thieves would not come back empty-handed, and Geraldine accepts them. Advice from Trickster, also passed on by Sver if Kir consults him, about an ice elemental in the abandoned mines provides something to offer Yam-Akara. His work and the governor’s permit requirements then draw the travellers into further dealings with the court. The missing nugget will matter again when the apparent caravan failure becomes evidence of a separate theft. Yam-Akara introduces himself as a practising magician of the first rank and an honorary member of the Assembly of Magicians of Three Worlds. The elemental samples interest him, and the Joon artifact promises material for a scholarly report. He agrees to search while Kir renews his permit for the mines, where Wormface magic interferes with his measurements. His summons the travellers to Governor Valrasian whether or not his own laboratory errand is complete. The governor demands proper introductions, pays unwelcome attention to Kel and hints at a rare Blue Clan mage’s dart for his collection. Bringing the dart wins the permit, despite his complaints about Yam-Akara’s visits. Kir can continue helping [[character/haburu]] after freeing the dogs kept near Karansul’s manufactories. The elder first rewards him with a clue to valuables behind a fence south of the city; Kir finds that he can crawl underneath. Khabburu then asks him to water a neglected tree beside the well in a military camp. Next he asks for a frightened animal from the village south of Karansul’s domain to be guided to the Woodsfolk. The animal is a cow, whose milk interests them. After these acts, Khabburu gives Kir a key dropped by a man he saw staggering and singing near the mines. The key helps solve the gates and levers barring an underground chest. Its contents include the third Rod of Life fragment. This chain is optional, but its completion can determine whether Kir later has the means to bring Kel back. Green leaves around the settlement lead Kir to Grey Leaf, who brings the news. Brissen is murdered and Yam-Akara is accused of killing his old friend. Kir and Kel undertake the defence. The magician says he spent the day in the mines and arrived late for their meeting. [[character/guard]] confirms that he allowed the elderly visitor through with an expired permit and stamped it that day. Kir finds the lost pass, but [[character/huber]] rejects the water-damaged document because the signature and date can no longer be read. This evidence supports the search but does not free Yam-Akara; the travellers still have to identify the murderer. A knife found at the murder site appears to implicate His. The court magician admits it was stolen from his laboratory together with the governor’s nugget. He had sent out the empty caravan to hide that loss and hoped to blame raiders after an informant warned of the planned attack. His arranges a meeting to produce evidence, but is killed before he can clear himself. Meanwhile Geraldine and Karansul disclose their relationship and provide each other with an alibi. Their commercial hostility and private secrecy had made them suspicious without establishing guilt. The settlement’s missing communal money supplies the decisive motive. Kir and Kel catch Crooked at his cache. Brissen had discovered the theft, so Crooked killed him. He also stole His’s knife and the gold nugget, informed on the caravan raid and later planted the knife to shift suspicion. His called the same informant to clear his own name; Crooked mistook that invitation for a trap and killed him too. Woodsfolk observations help reconstruct the planted evidence. Before the governor, Kir explains the connected crimes and Crooked admits them. Yam-Akara is released, while the governor reserves Crooked’s punishment for trial. Kel draws the thief out by spreading word that they have found the hidden money. Afterwards the travellers return the recovered communal funds to Geraldine and Trickster. Geraldine wants personal revenge, but Crooked is already in the governor’s custody. During his confinement, Yam-Akara gains access to the governor’s library. Old exploration reports reveal that the powerful “artifact” is a forgotten passage to another land. Trickster offers a key to the gate, then sends Kir on a fruitless ore search so that he can work without interference. With the key ready, Yam-Akara warns that he cannot sense the destination: the portal may be defective or concealed by a powerful absorbing spell. Kir recognises the same absence Tka-Rik described and concludes that it leads to Jigran. He decides to go directly, trusting the strength gained during his journey. Kel chooses to accompany him again. The old portal brings the travellers to the Canian side of Jigran, where [[character/baron]] questions their arrival amid attacks by the undead. The baron has lost Dar-Ulgorn to Firez’s forces but refuses Kir’s suggestion to seek outside help, citing his family’s pride. Kir and Kel assist the endangered settlements. They meet the baron’s son [[character/bson]] and the overworked [[character/stark]]. Stark provides a password for [[character/doctor]], a seller of sweets who secretly gathers intelligence for the baron. These local alliances make the campaign against Firez possible. The trail of the local undead leads to [[character/nekro]] on Death Island. Brought before the baron, he bargains for his life with the promise of useful knowledge. Kir and Kel obtain a potion from a tomb, but need to know how to apply it across the affected area. Jaminin first entertains a human sacrifice; Kel rejects it, and he supplies a less destructive method involving cemetery soil and an incantation. The potion puts the dead to rest. His later exchanges preserve the distinction between theoretical learning and practical competence: he possesses information, but his own experiment caused the disaster. Their success also changes the baron’s view of Kel. He admits that her achievements have repeatedly disproved his claim that war is no business for women. Dartas treats Kel as someone he is entitled to possess, insults her attachment to Kir and refuses to accept rejection. When Kir confronts him, Dartas asks what he wants in exchange for her and then calls him a coward. They duel on Death Island. Defeated and spared, Dartas admits despair over Dar-Ulgorn’s loss and his family’s future. Kir answers with his own enslavement, escape and determination to fight, winning Dartas’s respect. Kel initially believes the duel means that Kir has recognised her feelings; he disappoints her by calling it a defence of his own honour. The baron considers punishment, then accepts that Dartas needed the lesson; Kir asks him not to punish his son further. Kir proposes a special weapon alloy against the undead, drawing on a book he read. Stark sends him to an abandoned forge rather than allow a youngster to work in his own smithy. When Kir returns with the alloy, Kel recognises the source of the craftsman’s resistance: a hereditary master is ashamed of learning something his father never taught him. Kir presents the discovery as knowledge Stark can pass to his own son. The smith agrees to try it, and the baron welcomes the advantage for his soldiers. The improved weapons strengthen his preparations for an offensive. Rad leaves his troop report in a cemetery cache; collecting herbs gives him an innocent reason to visit it. Kir and Kel deliver the report, gather poisonous mushrooms and a pumpkin for Rad’s stew, then take the prepared meal to the enemy mess hall. The pumpkin prolongs the mushrooms’ laxative effect, keeping defenders away from their posts during the assault. Uncle Rad’s intelligence and preparations distract the defenders of Dar-Ulgorn so the baron’s forces can retake the fortress. The victory restores the family’s former boundary, but Virril will not advance blindly into Khadaganian territory. Kir and Kel steal a detailed map from the enemy headquarters and deliver Rad’s report. The resulting offensive captures the river crossing and brings Firez within reach. Kel worries that the end of Kir’s family quest will also end their life together, while the baron imagines a prosperous Jigran under his descendants. The victory means different things to the people who share it. Kel and Rad discover that Firez is moving the Joon prisoners from the mountain prison into his fortress. Kel plans an attack on the transfer, avoiding a direct prison assault. Among those freed are [[character/deva]], whom Kir admired as a child, and the elder [[character/junofil]]. Tai-Ilara welcomes his changed appearance and asks him to retrieve belongings left behind. Tui-Len brings harder news: Kir’s parents are dead. The elder fears that killing Firez will expose the survivors to the Curse, but Kir tells him that Tka-Rik and At-Zako have already destroyed it. Tui-Len also opens the sealed Joon cache whose amulet Kir has recovered. Seeing Kir reunited with Tai-Ilara, Kel asks for the way back to Suslanger. Kir begs her to stay and mentions one more expedition for Tai-Ilara’s belongings. Kel agrees because she still fears for him, calling it their last adventure together. She dies during that expedition. On Kir’s return, Tai-Ilara is concerned with her comb and mirror and dismisses his grief. Her reaction breaks his idealised childhood attachment. He recognises Kel as the person who was closest and most loyal to him, and realises that he failed to see her love while she was beside him. Kel can be resurrected in the original Lost in Astral campaign. Her scripted death still occurs, but if Kir has all three parts of the Rod of Life when he finishes the conversation with [[character/deva|Tai-Ilara]] about her retrieved belongings, [[character/junofil|Tui-Len]] offers to bring Kel back. Completing his conversation consumes the fragments and returns Kel alive to the playable party before the final battle, with her saved skills, experience and equipment. Speak to her afterward for their reunion: Kir finally declares his love and asks forgiveness for his blindness. Kel answers that his love matters more than everything else. The sealed cache supplies Kir with Joon armour, but Tui-Len warns him against relying on hatred alone. He gives him an amulet that can turn dangerous creatures into allies. Rad identifies suitable hunting grounds for a cyclops and a dragon. Their recruitment changes the military balance and answers the baron’s objection that his soldiers cannot face Firez’s necromancy in a direct assault. Virril finally orders the attack. Before the confrontation, Rad speaks of the quiet home and family he hopes to have when his secret work is finished. The cache is found in the valley Rad hopes to settle after the war. Dartas’s account of a nearby village destroyed by harpies points Kir to the rectangular amulet needed at its sealed entrance; Tui-Len supplies the remaining magical help. During the assault, Firez sends the city’s population, transformed into undead, against the Canian force. Kir must break through this army to reach the palace. In the throne room, Firez reveals that he too is a Joon and has watched Kir through a dragonet since the escape. He says his people expelled him for necromancy and claims that his rule protected them from the Curse. Kir answers with their enslavement, his parents’ deaths and the destruction of Jigran to prolong Firez’s life. The tyrant’s explanation is his own defence, not proof that the captivity was benevolent. He threatens to kill Kir, raise him as an obedient servant and use him against the baron. Their exchange leads into the final battle for Jigran. Firez shelters behind a lethal magical barrier. Kir disables its four controls before he can reach the necromancer; teleportation platforms and enchanted lion statues form part of the final arena. Killing Firez completes the last quest and ends the campaign.

entries.search: The Last Shelter is the fugitive brotherhood’s hidden refuge. Aliya brings Kir and Kel here, but Khatul tests them before granting trust. The smith’s change of attitude after acceptance makes membership a tangible part of life in the community. Feiruz asks Kir to repay his help by rescuing his imprisoned fiancée [[character/merc10]]. He dies during the escape. Kel urges the grieving Aliya to avenge him and identifies the man who struck the fatal blow. Kir objects to deliberate revenge, but their companions insist on their code. The death of the prison commandant brings searches across the city. Fearing for his collection, Rindeil withdraws his protection, though he says Kir may return once the danger passes. Aliya then leads Kir and Kel to the Last Shelter and speaks for them before [[character/glav]]. Khatul demands an imperial signet ring from a cyclops as a test of trust. Kir brings it back and explains his intention to free his family. He also recognises that the ring does not match the description he has read. Khatul already knows it is false, but asks him to preserve the brotherhood’s belief in the trophy. Membership changes how [[character/zaku]] receives Kir: the smith who refused a stranger now offers his craft. Through Aliya, Kir also searches for the missing [[character/merc7]], rescues her and brings medicine. Sahilia’s recovery matters later, when her forged papers open a route into the army. An imperial scout discovers the Shelter. After fighting the expedition, Khatul proposes placing Wormface bodies at the battlefield to conceal the brotherhood’s involvement. In the depths, [[character/guru]] recognises Kir as a Joon and invokes an ancient treaty. He demands the death of a necromancer disturbing the caves before granting access. Later he calls Kir mentally and offers information for rescuing the Priest of Silence from the necromancers. His account of a human searching for Joon remains gives another lead, though he cannot say where that man now lives. The alliance is reciprocal and conditional, not a promise to answer every question.

Bor claims neutrality in the war, yet asks them to act against the village’s hunters and caravans. To question [[character/smith]] about the Orb, Kir helps bring him out of the village. Further paid stories lead Kir to an animated skeleton’s severed legs in the Dead City and to a giant ogre being fattened by the island orcs. The ogre quest proposes overfeeding it: starving it would make it dangerous, while ordinary feeding would let it grow. At the end of this optional sequence, Kir notices the heavy object Uyka wears around her neck. She found it in the mountains and treats it as a possible charm against evil or lizards. Kir recognises it as a key and can buy it. It opens the way to the Hall of the Great in the lizardmen’s tomb, where the greatest chiefs were buried. Among its rewards is another fragment of the Rod of Life, giving Uyka’s local gossip a consequence far beyond Gipath.

entries.search: [[character/stark]] is the overworked master serving the Canian garrison. He claims inherited expertise in smithing, spellcraft and complex potions, and complains that people visit only when they need something. He introduces the travellers to Uncle Rad’s covert role and is intrigued by the unusual alloy they later bring him. The old portal brings the travellers to the Canian side of Jigran, where [[character/baron]] questions their arrival amid attacks by the undead. The baron has lost Dar-Ulgorn to Firez’s forces but refuses Kir’s suggestion to seek outside help, citing his family’s pride. Kir and Kel assist the endangered settlements. They meet the baron’s son [[character/bson]] and the overworked [[character/stark]]. Stark provides a password for [[character/doctor]], a seller of sweets who secretly gathers intelligence for the baron. These local alliances make the campaign against Firez possible. Kir proposes a special weapon alloy against the undead, drawing on a book he read. Stark sends him to an abandoned forge rather than allow a youngster to work in his own smithy. When Kir returns with the alloy, Kel recognises the source of the craftsman’s resistance: a hereditary master is ashamed of learning something his father never taught him. Kir presents the discovery as knowledge Stark can pass to his own son. The smith agrees to try it, and the baron welcomes the advantage for his soldiers. entries.search: On Gipath, [[character/orcc]] says his warriors destroyed the Khadaganian expedition. He remembers how Zak’s defeat of a supposed Demon showed that armoured outsiders could be killed, and hopes Kir will become a Chosen for his own tribe. Kel proposes a false report with unpromising stone samples to prevent another imperial expedition from being sent. The shaman [[character/orcpyr]] distrusts strangers but makes Kir a ritual axe after he supplies suitable stone, and makes beads for Kel. Their welcome depends on helping the tribe, and Kir soon rescues the chief from a harpy and his wife from goblins. Urk-Tar explains that humans have driven orcs out of the Foothills and are advancing into the Middle Mountains. Kir removes the Shell whose presence restrains the lizards, initially refusing to fight humans himself. When Tynachey describes the killing of the tribe’s inhabitants, Kel argues for helping their hosts recover the settlement, and Kir agrees. The [[character/iz|Hermit Lizard]] then offers news of the former Chosen in exchange for placing the Shell by the Remote Mountains’ lake. Restoring it also frees hunters held by lizards. The Hermit directs Kir toward the Great Magician by a route different from Zak’s old tunnel approach. Bor introduces Kir to [[character/spletnica]], who lives alone and receives household help in exchange for news. Her first story points toward the giant mushrooms near the goblin camp in the Middle Mountains; only one is edible. Later she reports that a survivor of the Khadaganian expedition left Estera’s refuge for the Distant Mountains. Kir worries that the man might return to Suslanger, and the resulting lead concerns treasure in the ruined expedition camp. Uyka also describes Go-Go as an imprisoned champion of goblin freedom and praises his supposed beauty. Kel is curious enough to consider visiting him, and the pair can free him from the island orcs. Uyka’s requests for repairs, provisions and money accompany these conversations; her account of someone’s motives or attractiveness remains her opinion. The stolen Orb stands on an island orc pedestal. Kir obtains the bridge gear from their gathering on Council Mountain to reach it. Once Babur is safe and has seen the damaged Orb, he provides the key to the observatory approach. The observatory book lets Estera prescribe washing the Orb in underground spring water. A landslide closes Kir’s former route to Tka-Rik, forcing him through the old tunnel. Before departure, Airy asks Kel to greet the Chosen if they meet him and says she still remembers him. Kel apologises for her earlier jealousy; both women recognise feelings Kir has yet to understand. The repaired Orb shows snow rather than Jigran. Tka-Rik interprets this as Ingos, agrees that Kel can go with Kir, and warns that greater freedom there does not prevent cruel government or make their search for powerful magic safe.

entries.search: Khatul demands an imperial signet ring from a cyclops as a test of trust. Kir brings it back and explains his intention to free his family. He also recognises that the ring does not match the description he has read. Khatul already knows it is false, but asks him to preserve the brotherhood’s belief in the trophy. Membership changes how [[character/zaku]] receives Kir: the smith who refused a stranger now offers his craft. Through Aliya, Kir also searches for the missing [[character/merc7]], rescues her and brings medicine. Sahilia’s recovery matters later, when her forged papers open a route into the army. An imperial scout discovers the Shelter. After fighting the expedition, Khatul proposes placing Wormface bodies at the battlefield to conceal the brotherhood’s involvement. In the depths, [[character/guru]] recognises Kir as a Joon and invokes an ancient treaty. He demands the death of a necromancer disturbing the caves before granting access. Later he calls Kir mentally and offers information for rescuing the Priest of Silence from the necromancers. His account of a human searching for Joon remains gives another lead, though he cannot say where that man now lives. The alliance is reciprocal and conditional, not a promise to answer every question. Karim locates a report about the missing red-skinned youth in the necromancers’ citadel. He has bribed a guard to open the gate and get the other guards drunk, but the watch remains alert. Kir and Kel retrieve the document despite the failed arrangement, and Kir defends Karim when Kel blames him. The report records transformation and teleportation before the attack on the scholars’ mansion, with Gipath as the destination. Kir decides to follow that Joon. Sahilia initially warns against joining the army, then has convincing enlistment papers forged while Kir empties her dangerous caches for her. Kel refuses to be left behind, passing as a young man herself. [[character/sergant]] puts them through military training in Death Canyon. Their performance earns a courier assignment to the Gipath expedition. Sealed orders and a portal pass finally let them leave Suslanger under the authority of the same empire that enslaved them.

[[character/hwleader]] dismisses his papers, treats him as a slave and considers reporting the red-skinned stranger for a reward.

entries.search: [[character/elder]] owns an estate on Suslanger and collects spiders. Kel knows him, and his scientific interests initially make him receptive to Kir. He asks Kir to obtain a meteorite sample that he intends to exchange for a rare specimen for his collection. His hospitality has limits: when soldiers begin searching after the prison commandant’s murder, he sends them away to protect himself and his collection. [[character/elder]] welcomes Kel and her companion to his estate. Kir’s learning gives them common ground, though the collector’s chief concern remains his spiders. [[character/sheriff]], who manages the household and formerly performed on stage, remembers a report about a red-skinned youth and promises to investigate. Rindeil’s hospitality gives the fugitives a base, but Kir realises that the slave records still identify them. With Rindeil’s guidance, he steals the records from the authorities. This removes one immediate threat without concealing his conspicuous appearance. Rindeil suggests a poison that would change Kir’s skin colour but could cause paralysis; Karim offers a recipe that would take months. Neither solves the urgent problem. [[character/merc8]] proposes wrapping Kir’s face in cloth: survivors of a recent disease already conceal their disfigurement that way. Kir helps him with a theft to obtain the fabric, and Feiruz rewards his assistance. The disguise initially fools even Rindeil. It lets Kir move among the Khadaganians while continuing the search for another Joon. When Kel returns, she mocks the expensive cloth as an extravagant way to impersonate a poor survivor. She also warns that Rindeil’s promises of help are less reliable than his interest in spiders, and rejoins Kir to keep others from taking advantage of him. Rindeil wants a meteorite sample brought from the lands the Khadaganians call useless. He has arranged to exchange it for a rare addition to his collection. Kir overhears the guards to locate the sample, but its locked chest calls for a better thief. Karim directs him to Feiruz at the Black Market. Kel challenges Feiruz’s pride until he agrees to help, on condition that they return the favour later. He opens the chest, earns Kel’s praise and leaves the party to rest. Rindeil rewards the delivery. The unpaid favour explains why Feiruz later expects help rescuing Aliya. Feiruz asks Kir to repay his help by rescuing his imprisoned fiancée [[character/merc10]]. He dies during the escape. Kel urges the grieving Aliya to avenge him and identifies the man who struck the fatal blow. Kir objects to deliberate revenge, but their companions insist on their code. The death of the prison commandant brings searches across the city. Fearing for his collection, Rindeil withdraws his protection, though he says Kir may return once the danger passes. Aliya then leads Kir and Kel to the Last Shelter and speaks for them before [[character/glav]].

entries.search: Bor introduces Kir to [[character/spletnica]], who lives alone and receives household help in exchange for news. Her first story points toward the giant mushrooms near the goblin camp in the Middle Mountains; only one is edible. Later she reports that a survivor of the Khadaganian expedition left Estera’s refuge for the Distant Mountains. Kir worries that the man might return to Suslanger, and the resulting lead concerns treasure in the ruined expedition camp. Uyka also describes Go-Go as an imprisoned champion of goblin freedom and praises his supposed beauty. Kel is curious enough to consider visiting him, and the pair can free him from the island orcs. Uyka’s requests for repairs, provisions and money accompany these conversations; her account of someone’s motives or attractiveness remains her opinion. Further paid stories lead Kir to an animated skeleton’s severed legs in the Dead City and to a giant ogre being fattened by the island orcs. The ogre quest proposes overfeeding it: starving it would make it dangerous, while ordinary feeding would let it grow. At the end of this optional sequence, Kir notices the heavy object Uyka wears around her neck. She found it in the mountains and treats it as a possible charm against evil or lizards. Kir recognises it as a key and can buy it. It opens the way to the Hall of the Great in the lizardmen’s tomb, where the greatest chiefs were buried. Among its rewards is another fragment of the Rod of Life, giving Uyka’s local gossip a consequence far beyond Gipath. [[character/daughter]] guards the cave while Estera is visiting the [[character/skd|Old Dragon]]. Her quarrel with Kel over a necklace exposes Kel’s jealousy and Kir’s failure to notice it. Airy refuses his courtship and suggests looking at the person already beside him. At the dragon’s lair, Estera is the troublesome visitor rather than a prisoner: she refuses to leave without information about a flower. Kir obtains it and the witch goes home. [[character/witch]] then admits the Orb was stolen by orcs; Airy identifies the islands and warns that it lost its power after its earlier use. Airy’s warning about the depleted Orb leads Kir towards the observatory. Babur can open the blocked approach, but first demands the Chosen’s knife, now a sacred relic. While Kir pursues the relic, island orcs raid the hunters’ camp and carry Babur away. They hand him to their ogre neighbours after his dealings with them turn sour. Kir obtains the two keys to the pit, frees the craftsman and escorts him back alive. Babur renounces further trade with the orcs. His rescue also lets Bor put forward a new plan against the settlers. The stolen Orb stands on an island orc pedestal. Kir obtains the bridge gear from their gathering on Council Mountain to reach it. Once Babur is safe and has seen the damaged Orb, he provides the key to the observatory approach. The observatory book lets Estera prescribe washing the Orb in underground spring water. A landslide closes Kir’s former route to Tka-Rik, forcing him through the old tunnel. Before departure, Airy asks Kel to greet the Chosen if they meet him and says she still remembers him. Kel apologises for her earlier jealousy; both women recognise feelings Kir has yet to understand. The repaired Orb shows snow rather than Jigran. Tka-Rik interprets this as Ingos, agrees that Kel can go with Kir, and warns that greater freedom there does not prevent cruel government or make their search for powerful magic safe.

entries.search: Kel and Rad discover that Firez is moving the Joon prisoners from the mountain prison into his fortress. Kel plans an attack on the transfer, avoiding a direct prison assault. Among those freed are [[character/deva]], whom Kir admired as a child, and the elder [[character/junofil]]. Tai-Ilara welcomes his changed appearance and asks him to retrieve belongings left behind. Tui-Len brings harder news: Kir’s parents are dead. The elder fears that killing Firez will expose the survivors to the Curse, but Kir tells him that Tka-Rik and At-Zako have already destroyed it. Tui-Len also opens the sealed Joon cache whose amulet Kir has recovered. Seeing Kir reunited with Tai-Ilara, Kel asks for the way back to Suslanger. Kir begs her to stay and mentions one more expedition for Tai-Ilara’s belongings. Kel agrees because she still fears for him, calling it their last adventure together. She dies during that expedition. On Kir’s return, Tai-Ilara is concerned with her comb and mirror and dismisses his grief. Her reaction breaks his idealised childhood attachment. He recognises Kel as the person who was closest and most loyal to him, and realises that he failed to see her love while she was beside him. The sealed cache supplies Kir with Joon armour, but Tui-Len warns him against relying on hatred alone. He gives him an amulet that can turn dangerous creatures into allies. Rad identifies suitable hunting grounds for a cyclops and a dragon. Their recruitment changes the military balance and answers the baron’s objection that his soldiers cannot face Firez’s necromancy in a direct assault. Virril finally orders the attack. Before the confrontation, Rad speaks of the quiet home and family he hopes to have when his secret work is finished. The cache is found in the valley Rad hopes to settle after the war. Dartas’s account of a nearby village destroyed by harpies points Kir to the rectangular amulet needed at its sealed entrance; Tui-Len supplies the remaining magical help. During the assault, Firez sends the city’s population, transformed into undead, against the Canian force. Kir must break through this army to reach the palace.

entries.search: The slave pen is where Kir and Kel first form their partnership. Kel helps the beaten newcomer, while the officials reduce the prisoners to labour assignments. Their conversations turn captivity into the starting point of an escape. Soldiers beat Kir nearly to death. In the slave pen, [[character/merc2]] nurses him back to consciousness, shortens his name to Kir and offers a partnership in escape. He initially hopes to explain the mistake to the authorities; the [[character/clerk|official]] instead assigns work according to the prisoners’ abilities. entries.search: Suslanger is a small, arid possession of Khadagan. Irrigation supports its farms, while harsh and corrupt authority coexists with criminal networks, smuggling and blackmail. Kir and Kel meet in its slave pen. Their escape leads through estates, thieves’ contacts, the Last Shelter and the search for information about the Joons before military papers provide a way to Gipath. Soldiers beat Kir nearly to death. In the slave pen, [[character/merc2]] nurses him back to consciousness, shortens his name to Kir and offers a partnership in escape. He initially hopes to explain the mistake to the authorities; the [[character/clerk|official]] instead assigns work according to the prisoners’ abilities. Kel has overheard that an officer possesses a map of the catacombs. Their escape coincides with the Horror’s attack on the slave camp: guards die and the camp burns. They obtain the map and take the catacombs out of the fortress area. Kel, usually so confident, admits her unease about the dark underground route. Once outside, Kel proposes refuge with an acquaintance who collects spiders. Their relationship begins in this shared dependence: Kir needs her local knowledge, and Kel needs a partner. [[character/elder]] welcomes Kel and her companion to his estate. Kir’s learning gives them common ground, though the collector’s chief concern remains his spiders. [[character/sheriff]], who manages the household and formerly performed on stage, remembers a report about a red-skinned youth and promises to investigate. Rindeil’s hospitality gives the fugitives a base, but Kir realises that the slave records still identify them. With Rindeil’s guidance, he steals the records from the authorities. This removes one immediate threat without concealing his conspicuous appearance. Rindeil suggests a poison that would change Kir’s skin colour but could cause paralysis; Karim offers a recipe that would take months. Neither solves the urgent problem. [[character/merc8]] proposes wrapping Kir’s face in cloth: survivors of a recent disease already conceal their disfigurement that way. Kir helps him with a theft to obtain the fabric, and Feiruz rewards his assistance. The disguise initially fools even Rindeil. It lets Kir move among the Khadaganians while continuing the search for another Joon. When Kel returns, she mocks the expensive cloth as an extravagant way to impersonate a poor survivor. She also warns that Rindeil’s promises of help are less reliable than his interest in spiders, and rejoins Kir to keep others from taking advantage of him. Rindeil wants a meteorite sample brought from the lands the Khadaganians call useless. He has arranged to exchange it for a rare addition to his collection. Kir overhears the guards to locate the sample, but its locked chest calls for a better thief. Karim directs him to Feiruz at the Black Market. Kel challenges Feiruz’s pride until he agrees to help, on condition that they return the favour later. He opens the chest, earns Kel’s praise and leaves the party to rest. Rindeil rewards the delivery. The unpaid favour explains why Feiruz later expects help rescuing Aliya. Kel introduces Kir to the widowed merchant [[character/ycf]]. Zara has sold forbidden goods, including a powder Kel bought for her mother, and a blackmailer threatens to report her. She asks the pair to deliver a letter and later the payment, citing her late husband’s belief in a merchant’s good name. The quest takes a harsher turn: Kir can keep the money, leave a message, track the blackmailer and kill him. Zara then pays an additional reward. Kir’s private reaction acknowledges that he has profited twice from her trouble. Zara next asks for news of an overdue caravan carrying contraband. If Kir arrives too late, the guards seize the forbidden goods. Recovering them in time still leaves the caravan destroyed. Without further evidence, the attack appears to be the work of animals; finding Tarik’s note points instead to Azbek. Tarik is Zara’s senior caravan driver. Following this lead involves overhearing the blackmailers, freeing him from captivity outside the city and escorting him back. Zara’s relief at his return is a possible outcome of this branch, not the result of every visit to the ruined caravan. Feiruz asks Kir to repay his help by rescuing his imprisoned fiancée [[character/merc10]]. He dies during the escape. Kel urges the grieving Aliya to avenge him and identifies the man who struck the fatal blow. Kir objects to deliberate revenge, but their companions insist on their code. The death of the prison commandant brings searches across the city. Fearing for his collection, Rindeil withdraws his protection, though he says Kir may return once the danger passes. Aliya then leads Kir and Kel to the Last Shelter and speaks for them before [[character/glav]]. Khatul demands an imperial signet ring from a cyclops as a test of trust. Kir brings it back and explains his intention to free his family. He also recognises that the ring does not match the description he has read. Khatul already knows it is false, but asks him to preserve the brotherhood’s belief in the trophy. Membership changes how [[character/zaku]] receives Kir: the smith who refused a stranger now offers his craft. Through Aliya, Kir also searches for the missing [[character/merc7]], rescues her and brings medicine. Sahilia’s recovery matters later, when her forged papers open a route into the army. An imperial scout discovers the Shelter. After fighting the expedition, Khatul proposes placing Wormface bodies at the battlefield to conceal the brotherhood’s involvement. In the depths, [[character/guru]] recognises Kir as a Joon and invokes an ancient treaty. He demands the death of a necromancer disturbing the caves before granting access. Later he calls Kir mentally and offers information for rescuing the Priest of Silence from the necromancers. His account of a human searching for Joon remains gives another lead, though he cannot say where that man now lives. The alliance is reciprocal and conditional, not a promise to answer every question. While travelling through Suslanger in human guise, Kir can buy a succession of predictions from the [[character/skelet|fortune-teller]]. She first points him toward an orchard near the Portal, then toward a public building and an underground route. Further hints concern a harvest basket on the plantations, a chest beyond a fenced property, and an estate where undead appear at night. Kir challenges her obscure language but continues to investigate. The last prediction concerns the Wormface underground passages and a choice among enchanted mechanisms. Solving that puzzle can yield one of the fragments later identified as parts of the Rod of Life. These optional discoveries require Kir to act on the clues; the fortune-teller explicitly speaks of what may happen, not an inevitable future. Karim locates a report about the missing red-skinned youth in the necromancers’ citadel. He has bribed a guard to open the gate and get the other guards drunk, but the watch remains alert. Kir and Kel retrieve the document despite the failed arrangement, and Kir defends Karim when Kel blames him. The report records transformation and teleportation before the attack on the scholars’ mansion, with Gipath as the destination. Kir decides to follow that Joon. Sahilia initially warns against joining the army, then has convincing enlistment papers forged while Kir empties her dangerous caches for her. Kel refuses to be left behind, passing as a young man herself. [[character/sergant]] puts them through military training in Death Canyon. Their performance earns a courier assignment to the Gipath expedition. Sealed orders and a portal pass finally let them leave Suslanger under the authority of the same empire that enslaved them.

entries.search: [[character/deva]] is the woman Kir remembers from his childhood on Jigran. After he rescues her, she asks him to retrieve her belongings. Kel dies during that expedition, and Tai-Ilara’s dismissive response destroys Kir’s idealised image of his old attachment. Her part in the story reveals what Kir had failed to recognise in Kel. Kel and Rad discover that Firez is moving the Joon prisoners from the mountain prison into his fortress. Kel plans an attack on the transfer, avoiding a direct prison assault. Among those freed are [[character/deva]], whom Kir admired as a child, and the elder [[character/junofil]]. Tai-Ilara welcomes his changed appearance and asks him to retrieve belongings left behind. Tui-Len brings harder news: Kir’s parents are dead. The elder fears that killing Firez will expose the survivors to the Curse, but Kir tells him that Tka-Rik and At-Zako have already destroyed it. Tui-Len also opens the sealed Joon cache whose amulet Kir has recovered. Seeing Kir reunited with Tai-Ilara, Kel asks for the way back to Suslanger. Kir begs her to stay and mentions one more expedition for Tai-Ilara’s belongings. Kel agrees because she still fears for him, calling it their last adventure together. She dies during that expedition. On Kir’s return, Tai-Ilara is concerned with her comb and mirror and dismisses his grief. Her reaction breaks his idealised childhood attachment. He recognises Kel as the person who was closest and most loyal to him, and realises that he failed to see her love while she was beside him.

entries.search: Tka-Rik’s underground home links the two campaigns. He explains that Zak and Lu-a-Jalla have left to travel, listens to Kir’s account of Jigran and interprets the Magic Orb. The resulting clue directs Kir and Kel to Ingos. Meeting [[character/rick]] gives Kir his first direct contact with a free Joon magician. Tka-Rik explains that At-Zako and Lu-a-Jalla are travelling together and that he himself remains bound to Gipath. He has never heard of Jigran. Kir tells him about Firez, his enslaved family and his promise to return. Learning that more Joons need help renews Tka-Rik’s purpose. Since he cannot locate the hidden allod unaided, he sends Kir to find the Magic Orb that At-Zako once used. Finding the magician therefore begins another investigation rather than immediately opening the road home. The stolen Orb stands on an island orc pedestal. Kir obtains the bridge gear from their gathering on Council Mountain to reach it. Once Babur is safe and has seen the damaged Orb, he provides the key to the observatory approach. The observatory book lets Estera prescribe washing the Orb in underground spring water. A landslide closes Kir’s former route to Tka-Rik, forcing him through the old tunnel. Before departure, Airy asks Kel to greet the Chosen if they meet him and says she still remembers him. Kel apologises for her earlier jealousy; both women recognise feelings Kir has yet to understand. The repaired Orb shows snow rather than Jigran. Tka-Rik interprets this as Ingos, agrees that Kel can go with Kir, and warns that greater freedom there does not prevent cruel government or make their search for powerful magic safe.

entries.search: This meeting place belongs to Uncle Rad, the sweets seller who secretly serves the baron. A password from Stark opens a channel for intelligence and practical help, including the search for powerful allies outside the cities. The old portal brings the travellers to the Canian side of Jigran, where [[character/baron]] questions their arrival amid attacks by the undead. The baron has lost Dar-Ulgorn to Firez’s forces but refuses Kir’s suggestion to seek outside help, citing his family’s pride. Kir and Kel assist the endangered settlements. They meet the baron’s son [[character/bson]] and the overworked [[character/stark]]. Stark provides a password for [[character/doctor]], a seller of sweets who secretly gathers intelligence for the baron. These local alliances make the campaign against Firez possible. Rad’s trade made him a spy. Children from households on both sides of Jigran visited his shop and repeated things they had heard; through them he learned that the Khadaganians were preparing to attack Dar-Ulgorn. He warned the baron in time to limit the losses. He continues supplying sweets to Firez’s household and listening to customers, using the ordinary movements of a confectioner as cover. He also directs Kir towards Jaminin on Death Island: fighting each risen corpse will not stop the source of the outbreak. Rad leaves his troop report in a cemetery cache; collecting herbs gives him an innocent reason to visit it. Kir and Kel deliver the report, gather poisonous mushrooms and a pumpkin for Rad’s stew, then take the prepared meal to the enemy mess hall. The pumpkin prolongs the mushrooms’ laxative effect, keeping defenders away from their posts during the assault. Uncle Rad’s intelligence and preparations distract the defenders of Dar-Ulgorn so the baron’s forces can retake the fortress. The victory restores the family’s former boundary, but Virril will not advance blindly into Khadaganian territory. Kir and Kel steal a detailed map from the enemy headquarters and deliver Rad’s report. The resulting offensive captures the river crossing and brings Firez within reach. Kel worries that the end of Kir’s family quest will also end their life together, while the baron imagines a prosperous Jigran under his descendants. The victory means different things to the people who share it. The sealed cache supplies Kir with Joon armour, but Tui-Len warns him against relying on hatred alone. He gives him an amulet that can turn dangerous creatures into allies. Rad identifies suitable hunting grounds for a cyclops and a dragon. Their recruitment changes the military balance and answers the baron’s objection that his soldiers cannot face Firez’s necromancy in a direct assault. Virril finally orders the attack. Before the confrontation, Rad speaks of the quiet home and family he hopes to have when his secret work is finished. The cache is found in the valley Rad hopes to settle after the war. Dartas’s account of a nearby village destroyed by harpies points Kir to the rectangular amulet needed at its sealed entrance; Tui-Len supplies the remaining magical help. During the assault, Firez sends the city’s population, transformed into undead, against the Canian force. Kir must break through this army to reach the palace.

He says his people expelled him for necromancy and claims that his rule protected them from the Curse. Their exchange leads into the final battle for Jigran. Firez shelters behind a lethal magical barrier. entries.search: [[character/junofil]] is a Joon elder held under Firez’s rule. He explains that fear of the Curse led his people to trust Firez’s promises, and tells Kir that his parents are dead. After his liberation he opens a sealed Joon cave, counsels against hatred and gives advice about allies and the Rod of Life. Kel and Rad discover that Firez is moving the Joon prisoners from the mountain prison into his fortress. Kel plans an attack on the transfer, avoiding a direct prison assault. Among those freed are [[character/deva]], whom Kir admired as a child, and the elder [[character/junofil]]. Tai-Ilara welcomes his changed appearance and asks him to retrieve belongings left behind. Tui-Len brings harder news: Kir’s parents are dead. The elder fears that killing Firez will expose the survivors to the Curse, but Kir tells him that Tka-Rik and At-Zako have already destroyed it. Tui-Len also opens the sealed Joon cache whose amulet Kir has recovered. Seeing Kir reunited with Tai-Ilara, Kel asks for the way back to Suslanger. Kir begs her to stay and mentions one more expedition for Tai-Ilara’s belongings. Kel agrees because she still fears for him, calling it their last adventure together. She dies during that expedition. On Kir’s return, Tai-Ilara is concerned with her comb and mirror and dismisses his grief. Her reaction breaks his idealised childhood attachment. He recognises Kel as the person who was closest and most loyal to him, and realises that he failed to see her love while she was beside him. entries.search: [[character/ycf]] is a widowed merchant on Suslanger whose business draws Kir and Kel into contraband, blackmail and a missing caravan. Her later requests mix commerce with personal affection: she wants Kehel’s standing damaged to favour a scholar she loves. Her claims and suspicions form leads to investigate, rather than automatic proof against the people she names. Kel introduces Kir to the widowed merchant [[character/ycf]]. Zara has sold forbidden goods, including a powder Kel bought for her mother, and a blackmailer threatens to report her. She asks the pair to deliver a letter and later the payment, citing her late husband’s belief in a merchant’s good name. The quest takes a harsher turn: Kir can keep the money, leave a message, track the blackmailer and kill him. Zara then pays an additional reward. Kir’s private reaction acknowledges that he has profited twice from her trouble. Zara next asks for news of an overdue caravan carrying contraband. If Kir arrives too late, the guards seize the forbidden goods. Recovering them in time still leaves the caravan destroyed. Without further evidence, the attack appears to be the work of animals; finding Tarik’s note points instead to Azbek. Tarik is Zara’s senior caravan driver. Following this lead involves overhearing the blackmailers, freeing him from captivity outside the city and escorting him back. Zara’s relief at his return is a possible outcome of this branch, not the result of every visit to the ruined caravan. Later, Zara falls in love with an imperial scholar. She regards Kehel as the rival obstructing his work and his claim to lead the Necromancers’ Guild. Her solution is to give Kir a special scroll with which to discredit Kehel before the guild. The successful return conversation records her gratitude. Her allegations about Kehel come from a lover supporting her chosen man; they do not establish an impartial account of the scholars’ dispute.
